Un prêt français à la Mauritanie : 21 millions d’euros pour le soutien de la formation professionnelle et le renforcement des capacités de la protection civile
items.description: Deux accords de financement ont été signés ce lundi à Nouakchott entre la Mauritanie et la France destinés, à soutenir la formation professionnelle et renforcer les capacités de la protection civile en Mauritanie. Ces accords prévoient un prêt d'un montant de 21 millions d'euros, soit environ 944 millions MRU. Les deux accords ont été signés par le ministre mauritanien des Affaires économiques et du Développement, Mouhamedou Ahmedou Mhaimid, en présence de l’ambassadeur de France en Mauritanie, Emmanuel Besnier, et du directeur de l’Agence française de développement à Nouakchott, Inias Monkam Davirat. Selon l’Agence mauritanienne d’information (officielle), ces deux accords contribuent « au financement d’un projet visant à soutenir la protection civile en renforçant ses capacités et sa résilience, à assurer la sécurité de la population face aux différents risques, ainsi qu’à un protocole d’accord d’une valeur de 4 millions d’euros, soit environ 180 millions de nouvelles ouguiyas, destiné à financer un projet de soutien à l’école d’enseignement technique et de formation professionnelle industrielle de Nouakchott. » Le ministre des Affaires économiques et du Développement a déclaré que « la signature de ces deux accords constitue une avancée dans le renforcement de la coopération entre la Mauritanie et la France dans les domaines de la protection civile, de l’enseignement technique et de la formation professionnelle ». Il a salué « le niveau de coopération entre les deux pays ainsi que le soutien apporté par l’Agence française de développement aux programmes nationaux de développement, qui s’est étendu à l’éducation, à la formation professionnelle, à la décentralisation, à la sécurité alimentaire, à la santé et à l’allègement de la dette ».

items.title: Burkina Faso minister impressed by Ghanaian crafts ahead of Ghana Day at SIAO 2026
items.description: Burkina Faso’s Minister for Industry, Commerce and Crafts, Serge Gnaidem Poda, has praised the quality and diversity of Ghanaian artefacts and crafts on display at the 18th International Arts and Handicraft Trade Show of Ouagadougou (SIAO 2026). Mr Poda made the remarks during a visit to the Ghana Village Pavilion on Monday, November 2, 2026, ahead of Ghana Day celebrations scheduled for Tuesday, November 3. He was accompanied by officials of his ministry and traditional rulers and was received by Ghana’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso, Kenneth Akibate, who highlighted the significance of Ghana’s participation in the international exhibition. The Burkina Faso minister expressed admiration for the creativity, craftsmanship and variety of the items on display, saying they reflected Ghana’s rich cultural heritage and the ingenuity of its artisans. Earlier, Ghana’s Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, had encouraged participants and visitors at SIAO 2026 to visit the pavilion and experience Ghana’s cultural identity through its traditional crafts and artefacts.

items.title: What Is Wrong With Us: Africa cannot blame its way to economic freedom
items.description: Our grievances against history are real, and the world owes us honesty about them. But a continent that spends its finest energy assigning blame may one morning discover that the past has been thoroughly explained while the future has been left entirely unbuilt. By Ing. Prof. Douglas Boateng, Chartered Director UK | Chartered Engineer UK | Fellow, Institute of Directors UK | Fellow, Ghana Institution of Engineering | Governance, Industrialisation and Supply Chain Strategist | Founder, Boardroom Governance Summit | Founder and Scriber, NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) The Continent With An Answer For Everything A remarkable talent has quietly flourished across our continent, and it is the ability to explain almost any problem with breathtaking precision. We know who caused it, which administration inherited it, which one worsened it, which international institution contributed to it and which foreign power ought to apologise for it. We can debate yesterday’s mistakes for hours, form committees to investigate them, and, when those committees report, form fresh committees to discover why the first recommendations were never implemented. Meanwhile the drain remains blocked, the factory stays shut, the graduate is still unemployed, the farmer still cannot reach the market, and an African child is still waiting for a future promised before her parents were born. There is, however, a profound difference between understanding responsibility and becoming comfortably addicted to blame. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) draws the line gently: “blame may explain how we arrived at the crossroads, but only responsibility decides whether we remain standing there.” History Is A Teacher, Not A Permanent Address Let us begin with honesty, because Africa’s grievances are not imaginary. The transatlantic slave trade devastated communities across generations, colonial rule redirected wealth and institutions towards distant capitals, borders drawn with a ruler cut through kinship and commerce alike, and an unequal global financial architecture still narrows the choices of many African economies. Yet honesty must travel in both directions. Ghana became independent in 1957, Nigeria in 1960 and Kenya in 1963, which means many African nations have now governed themselves for well over six decades, while South Africa, whose democracy dates from 1994, carries a more recent and distinctive legacy of exclusion. The uncomfortable question is how much of today’s underperformance flows from inherited structures and how much from decisions, institutions and behaviours firmly within our own control. Asking that question does not absolve anyone abroad; it simply refuses to surrender African agency, for a continent cannot demand sovereignty while outsourcing responsibility for its choices. As NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) reminds us, “the past may explain the weight upon our shoulders, but it must not forever choose the direction of our footsteps.” Rich In Resources, Poor In Value Africa holds vast mineral wealth, abundant arable land, extraordinary solar potential and the youngest population on earth, yet these blessings have not automatically become broad prosperity. The International Energy Agency estimates that roughly 600 million Africans still live without electricity. The contradiction is almost poetic in its cruelty. We mine the cobalt that powers the world’s smartphones while our own businesses run on generators, we export raw cocoa and import the chocolate at many times the price, and we educate brilliant young people who too often discover that their best opportunities lie on another continent. Global market structures certainly matter, but so do our energy policies, procurement decisions, industrial strategies and institutional discipline. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) observes that “a nation that exports its opportunities as raw materials should not be surprised when prosperity returns wearing somebody else’s label.” Ghana And The River That Nobody Poisoned Ghana offers a familiar illustration. Successive governments have wrestled with debt, infrastructure gaps, youth unemployment and environmental degradation. The difficulty arises when public debate becomes a tournament to decide which administration deserves the larger share of blame, while the citizen simply wants reliable power, clean water, affordable transport, good schools and the chance to earn a dignified living. Consider illegal mining, which has turned once pristine rivers the colour of strong tea. Government must enforce the law, protect water bodies, prosecute wrongdoing and offer credible livelihoods, but we must also ask who supplies the excavators, who finances the operations, who buys the gold, who provides local protection and who stays silent because a relative is profiting. The answers reveal that responsibility stretches far beyond the government of the day. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) puts it sharply: “when everyone condemns the polluted river but nobody questions what is poisoning it, outrage becomes merely another form of entertainment.” Arguing About The Builder While The Roof Leaks Nigeria shows the vast distance between possessing potential and converting it into productivity, for a nation whose entrepreneurs have built celebrated businesses in finance, technology and entertainment still loses enormous output to unreliable electricity, infrastructure bottlenecks and policy uncertainty. South Africa, meanwhile, carries the deep structural inequalities of apartheid, which rightly demand sustained attention, yet its experience of load shedding, faltering municipal services and the extensive governance failures documented by the Zondo Commission into state capture shows why historical explanation must always travel alongside present accountability. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) captures the point with homely wisdom: “history may explain why the house needs repairs, but it cannot excuse leaving the roof leaking while the caretakers argue about the original builder.” The Shortcuts We Condemn In Public And Seek In Private Picture an ordinary neighbourhood after heavy rain, a scene that mirrors how we often treat taxes, public property and the little envelope that hurries a file along. Residents rightly blame the authorities for inadequate drainage, yet some of those same residents have been emptying refuse into gutters and tolerating buildings on waterways for years, so when the flood arrives everybody demands accountability and almost nobody volunteers a confession. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) is unsparing here: “a society cannot keep demanding honest institutions while privately rewarding the shortcuts that make them dishonest.” Fairness requires a careful distinction, however, because citizens cannot be expected to resist corruption without protection. Afrobarometer’s 2026 survey across 38 countries found that among those who sought the services, 29 percent reported paying a bribe for an identity document and 22 percent for medical care. A mother pressured to pay for her child’s treatment does not carry the same responsibility as the official who exploits her desperation. Accountability Must Begin Where Power Sits Calls for personal responsibility must never become a convenient alibi for failed leadership. A farmer cannot build a national irrigation network, a student cannot single handedly reform an education system, so those who control budgets, legislation and enforcement agencies carry a correspondingly heavier burden. Africans understand this well, and Afrobarometer’s 2026 findings show that 59 percent of respondents across 38 countries prefer accountable government even if it slows decisions, over speedier decisions with less citizen involvement. Every major public programme should therefore carry measurable objectives, transparent budgets, named institutional owners and published results, while audit findings must produce corrective action, procurement irregularities must be investigated consistently, appointments must reward competence, and consequences must apply regardless of political colours. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) offers a useful definition: “accountability is not the punishment of political opponents, but the consistent application of standards, especially when the wrongdoer wears our own party’s shirt.” What Seoul, Singapore And Tallinn Did Not Do South Korea, Singapore and Estonia appear so often in development speeches that they deserve honorary citizenship of every African conference centre, and while their histories and circumstances differ greatly from ours and should never be copied mechanically, their lessons are instructive. In 1960, South Korea and Ghana had broadly comparable incomes per person, and Korea’s divergence came from decades of patient investment in skills, manufacturing and disciplined implementation. Singapore paired world class public administration with relentless execution, and Estonia built digital public services that dismantled bureaucratic barriers. As NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) reminds us, “wisdom does not require copying another traveller’s journey; it requires understanding which habits carried them to their destination.” From Explanations To Execution What, then, must change? Governments should publish annual development scorecards showing what was promised, funded, completed and independently verified, while parliaments should pursue audit findings until they are resolved rather than allowing them to retire peacefully in institutional archives. Businesses should measure success through productive investment, decent employment, tax compliance and environmental stewardship. Schools should teach civic responsibility alongside literacy, numeracy and technical skill, communities should organise around practical improvements such as cleaner streets and safer roads, and citizens should judge policies by evidence rather than by the party that proposed them. Continental bodies, for their part, should prize implementation milestones in infrastructure, industrialisation and regional trade above the elegance of their communiqués. Above all, we must change the questions we ask, moving from who caused the problem to who has the authority to fix it, and from demanding integrity of others to examining whether our own conduct strengthens the standards we preach. The Question Each Of Us Must Answer The world will not stop competing because Africa has legitimate grievances, technology will not wait while we finish the argument, and the next generation will not remain young while today’s leaders debate yesterday’s failures. We must therefore hold leaders accountable without surrendering personal responsibility, demand international fairness without abandoning domestic reform, and confront structural injustice without excusing corruption, incompetence or indiscipline. Economic freedom is not merely the absence of external control; it is the presence of productive capacity, credible institutions and opportunity shared widely enough that every citizen has a stake in its success. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) leaves us with a final reflection: “the past deserves truth, the present demands responsibility and the future requires action, for a generation that spends its life assigning blame may bequeath its children the same problems, accompanied only by better explanations.” Africa cannot blame its way to economic freedom; it must build, produce, govern, learn and cooperate its way there. And if we already know so much about what is wrong with us, the most uncomfortable question remains: what am I personally prepared to do differently, beginning tomorrow morning? ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ing. Professor Douglas Boateng is a pioneering international industrial, manufacturing and production systems engineer, governance strategist and Pan-African thought leader whose work continues to influence boardroom thinking, supply chain transformation and industrialisation strategy across the continent and beyond. As Africa’s first appointed Professor Extraordinaire in Supply Chain Management, he has long championed the integration of procurement, value chain development, industrialisation and governance into national and continental development agendas. An International Chartered Director and Chartered Engineer, he has received numerous lifetime achievement awards and authored several authoritative books. He is the scribe of the globally acclaimed NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom). His work rests on the conviction that Africa’s transformation — and the protection of its children — will come through deliberate action, strong institutions and leaders willing to build for generations they will never meet. © 2026 Ing. items.description: Le site des personnes déplacées de l'ISP, situé dans le quartier Muzipela à Bunia, traverse une grave crise d'approvisionnement en eau potable. Avec une population estimée à près de 16 000 personnes, le camp ne dispose que d'une seule source d'eau, insuffisante pour couvrir les besoins des milliers de ménages qui y vivent. Les déplacés redoutent les conséquences sanitaires de cette situation et sollicitent une intervention urgente des partenaires humanitaires.

items.title: 2027: 42 trade unions in Delta back Tinubu, Oborevwori, Dafinone
items.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16, elections, a coalition of 42 trade unions in Delta State has pledged support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎The coalition, operating under the Delta State Informal Sector Association, comprises over 120,000 artisans and informal sector workers across the state. ‎ ‎The group pledged its allegiance at the weekend when its leadership paid a solidarity visit to Senator representing Delta Central Senatorial District, Ede Dafinone. ‎ ‎While receiving the representatives of the association, Senator Dafinone described their coming together under one platform as a significant step towards strengthening grassroots mobilisation and political engagement. ‎ ‎He commended the various trade unions for uniting under the association and appreciated them for reaffirming their support for Tinubu, Oborevwori, his own re-election and the success of all APC candidates in the 2027 elections. ‎ ‎The senator said “this development reflects a shared commitment to strengthening our party’s political structures through effective grassroots mobilisation and sustained engagement with different segments of society.” ‎ ‎He also acknowledged the importance of the informal sector, noting that the coalition’s broad membership provided an avenue for deeper engagement with artisans, traders and other workers across Delta State. items.title: WILDAF-Togo échange avec des acteurs sur l’accès des femmes au droit et à la justice
items.description: Sokodé, 2 nov. (ATOP) – L’ONG « Women in Law and dévelopment in Africa » (WILDAF-Togo) a échangé avec les différents acteurs régionaux de la Centrale, les 29 et 30 octobre à Sokodé, sur l’accès des femmes au droit et à la justice avec un focus sur les Violences basées sur le genre (VBG). La rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet DeZon et du sous-projet « Appui au Leadership des Femmes et Jeunes Filles au Togo par l’Accès au Droit et à la Justice (PALJADJ) ». Ce projet, financé par la coopération allemande, est mis en œuvre par la GIZ, en collaboration avec le ministère des Solidarités, du Genre, de la Famille et de la Protection de l’Enfance. L’atelier vise à contribuer à l’amélioration de l’accès des femmes au droit et à la justice, notamment dans les situations de VBG. Les participants ont analysé et identifié les principaux obstacles liés à l’accès des femmes et filles au droit et à la justice. Les besoins et difficultés spécifiques de celles victimes ou exposées aux VBG en matière d’accès au droit et aux mécanismes de recours ont été répertoriés. Les séminaristes ont examiné le rôle et les complémentarités des différents acteurs dans l’information, l’orientation, le référencement, la protection et l’accompagnement des femmes dans leurs démarches de recours. Ils ont partagé les expériences et bonnes pratiques développées en matière d’accès au droit et à la justice pour la gente féminine. Les acteurs ont identifié et proposé une problématique relative à l’accès de des filles et des femmes au droit et à la justice pouvant faire l’objet d’une action de plaidoyer. La directrice exécutive de WILDAF-Togo, Mme Kpedji Anne Colette a souligné la nécessité de renforcer les mécanismes permettant aux femmes et filles victimes ou exposées aux violences de connaître leurs droits, d’accéder aux services compétents et de bénéficier de voies de recours adaptées. Officiels et participants. Le chef division Actions sociales, Tangbandja Gbati a salué WILDAF Togo et son partenaire pour cette initiative qui vient en appui aux actions gouvernementales en matière de promotion des droits des femmes et de l’éducation de la jeune fille dans le pays. Il a relevé que cette rencontre contribuera, non seulement, à relever les défis pour un meilleur accès des femmes au droit et à la justice mais aussi à mettre fin aux VBG. Le secrétaire général de la mairie de Tchaoudjo 1, Gmakagni Nikabou s’est réjoui de cette occasion donnée aux OSC d’évoquer les difficultés rencontrées sur le terrain et de formuler des propositions concrètes susceptibles d’améliorer la prévention des VBG ainsi que l’accès effectif de la gente féminine au droit et à la justice. Après Lomé, Tsévié et Atakpamé, Sokodé est la quatrième étape de cette rencontre d’échanges, qui se poursuit dans les deux autres régions du pays. ATOP/TAA/MEK/MD

items.title: Centrale : apothéose de la 7e édition du « mois du consommer local »
items.description: Sotouboua, 2 nov. (ATOP) – L’apothéose de la 7ᵉ édition du « Mois du consommer local » s’est déroulée, le vendredi 26 octobre à Sotouboua, pour le compte de la région Centrale, autour du thème : « Consommation locale, facteur d’intégration régionale et de souveraineté économique : défis et opportunités ». Cette édition est organisée par le ministère en charge du Commerce et du Contrôle de la qualité, en collaboration avec la Commission de l’UEMOA. Elle a permis de sensibiliser les populations sur l’importance de privilégier les produits « Made in Togo » et d’encourager les acteurs économiques à promouvoir la production, la transformation et la commercialisation des biens et services locaux. La célébration permet de mettre l’accent sur le rôle de la consommation locale dans le développement économique, la création d’emplois et l’amélioration des revenus des producteurs, artisans et transformateurs. Elle offre également l’occasion de mettre en lumière les richesses et les potentialités économiques du Togo, tout en encourageant les consommateurs à accorder une place de choix aux produits fabriqués sur le territoire national. Le thème retenu souligne les liens entre la consommation locale, l’intégration régionale et la souveraineté économique. En valorisant les produits locaux, les acteurs économiques contribuent au renforcement des échanges commerciaux, à la compétitivité des entreprises nationales et à la réduction de la dépendance vis-à-vis des importations. Toutefois, la promotion de cette consommation reste confrontée à plusieurs défis, notamment l’amélioration de la qualité des produits, leur accessibilité, leur compétitivité et leur visibilité sur les marchés. La sensibilisation des consommateurs ainsi que l’accompagnement des producteurs, des artisans et des petites entreprises sont essentiels pour renforcer la confiance envers les produits locaux. Au-delà des artisans, ce sont les producteurs, les commerçants et les consommateurs qui sont appelés à se mobiliser davantage autour d’un objectif commun : faire de la consommation locale un véritable levier de développement durable, d’intégration régionale et de souveraineté économique. Selon les organisateurs, consommer local, c’est soutenir les producteurs nationaux, valoriser le savoir-faire togolais et contribuer à la construction d’une économie plus forte et plus autonome. La cérémonie apothéose a pris fin par la visite des stands d’exposition des produits « Made in Togo » (agroalimentaire, artisanat, textile, cosmétique, service et innovation) par les autorités civiles et militaires présentes. ATOP/BTP/MEK/MD

items.title: NDLEA, Australian police sign pact against drug cartels
items.description: ….Marwa describes agreement as declaration of war on transnational traffickers By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) and the Australian Federal Police (AFP) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation against transnational drug trafficking networks operating along the Nigeria-Australia route. The agreement, signed at the NDLEA national headquarters in Abuja on Monday, November 2, 2026, formalises existing cooperation between the two agencies into a structured strategic partnership. Speaking at the ceremony, NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), described the agreement as “a declaration of war against transnational drug cartels that think they can hide between continents”. He expressed confidence that the partnership would make the Australia-Nigeria drug route hostile and unprofitable for traffickers, leveraging the AFP’s global reach and the NDLEA’s operational capacity. Under the agreement, the agencies will cooperate in four key areas: information and intelligence sharing, joint and coordinated operations, capacity building and professional development, and controlled delivery. Marwa said the pact came at a time when drug trafficking had become increasingly transnational, organised and sophisticated, with Nigerian organised crime groups allegedly linked to the Australia-Pacific drug route, particularly in the trafficking of methamphetamine and cocaine. “Nigeria is being exploited as a transit and sourcing hub, but no single country can fight this alone,” he said. He expressed hope that the agreement would lead to major joint seizures, arrests of high-value targets and successful controlled deliveries, adding that both agencies looked forward to its immediate implementation. Citing recent operations, the NDLEA boss disclosed that the agency had seized 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine intended for export and dismantled four methamphetamine laboratories in recent months, where Mexican nationals were allegedly embedded. He said one of the laboratories yielded seizures valued at more than $360 million. Marwa also cited the dismantling of a Switzerland-based cartel allegedly linked to a Nigerian, Simon Amadi, following more than a year of joint operations involving the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), as well as French, Greek and Swiss police. He said the cartel’s assets in Nigeria had also been targeted. In her remarks, leader of the AFP delegation, Ms Sandra Booth, said tackling drug trafficking required a whole-of-society approach. She commended the NDLEA for addressing different aspects of the problem, from prevention to enforcement, and described its international partnerships as commendable. Booth said the agreement would serve as a “force multiplier” in the fight against drug trafficking. She explained that organised crime groups increasingly used proceeds from drug trafficking to finance other serious crimes through what she described as a “crime as a service” model. According to her, young and vulnerable people are being drawn into criminal activities, including drug delivery and transportation, as well as violent attacks on rival groups. Beyond addiction and its effects on families and communities, she said drug trafficking was contributing to violence, gang conflicts and deaths in Australia. “Whilst Nigeria is a transit country, we are a destination country. And unfortunately for us, people will pay a lot of money for the commodity,” she said. Booth said Australia was committed to working with Nigeria to prevent drug trafficking and protect its young and vulnerable population. “It is so absolutely necessary that we work together as a team, that we are forceful, that we are committed, that we show integrity, and we hunt as a pack. And I am very proud that we can now be part of your pack,” she said. The ceremony was attended by the Australian High Commissioner to Nigeria, Ms Leilani Bin-Juda; Deputy High Commissioner, Timothy Milikan; other members of the AFP delegation, Andrea Humphrys and Susan Gray; and senior NDLEA officials. items.title: LONAGUI : deux parieurs remportent chacun 300 millions GNF et reçoivent officiellement leurs chèques en moins de 24 heures
items.description: La Loterie nationale de Guinée (LONAGUI) a procédé, ce lundi 2 novembre 2026, à la remise officielle des chèques à deux de ses parieurs ayant chacun remporté la somme de 300 millions de francs guinéens grâce au jeu « Extra 7-5 numéros » de l’Auto-Fortune. La cérémonie s’est déroulée au siège de l’institution, situé dans la commune de Dixinn, en présence des deux heureux gagnants et des responsables de la société. Il s’agit d’Ansoumane Camara et de Mohamed Diallo, qui ont chacun décroché ce gain exceptionnel à l’issue des tirages du week-end dernier. Un moment de grande émotion pour les deux bénéficiaires, qui n’ont pas caché leur joie après avoir reçu leurs chèques. Visiblement ému, Ansoumane Camara, qui affirme participer aux jeux de la LONAGUI depuis deux ans, a exprimé sa reconnaissance et son bonheur de vivre une telle expérience. « Je m'appelle Ansman Camara. Cela fait maintenant deux ans que je joue aux jeux de la Lonagui. Aujourd'hui, Dieu m'a fait grâce de remporter une somme de 300 millions de francs guinéens. Je suis vraiment très heureux. C'est un jour exceptionnel dans ma vie. Je peux même dire que c'est aujourd'hui que je ressens une telle joie. Je suis très, très content de ce qui m'arrive », a-t-il déclaré. Au-delà de la joie suscitée par ce gain, le nouveau millionnaire a également adressé un message d'encouragement aux autres parieurs, tout en souhaitant rassurer ceux qui doutent de la réalité des gains proposés par la LONAGUI. « Aux autres parieurs, je voudrais leur adresser un message d'encouragement. Je les invite à garder espoir. Qu'ils continuent à tenter leur chance, car peut-être que demain, Dieu leur accordera à leur tour une opportunité de gagner une somme encore plus importante que la mienne. Concernant ceux qui doutent de la réalité des gains de la Lonagui, je peux témoigner aujourd'hui que ces gains sont bien réels. Je ne suis certes pas la première personne à avoir remporté une telle somme, mais aujourd'hui, je suis moi-même la preuve que cela arrive réellement. Ce que je voyais peut-être chez les autres, je viens de le vivre à mon tour », a-t-il témoigné. Pour l'utilisation de cette importante somme, Ansoumane Camara envisage de se lancer dans l'entrepreneuriat et dans le secteur de la construction, deux projets qu'il souhaite concrétiser afin de mieux préparer son avenir. Même satisfaction chez Mohamed Diallo, deuxième bénéficiaire de ce gain de 300 millions de francs guinéens. Participant régulièrement aux jeux de la LONAGUI depuis plus de trois ans, il dit avoir été agréablement surpris par cette victoire qu'il n'imaginait pas forcément. « Je suis vraiment très content et heureux d'avoir remporté cette somme de 300 millions de francs guinéens. C'est une immense joie pour moi de vivre un tel moment. Je remercie sincèrement les responsables de la Lonagui pour cette opportunité. Cela fait maintenant plus de trois ans que je participe régulièrement aux jeux de la Lonagui. Durant tout ce temps, je continuais à tenter ma chance, sans jamais imaginer que je pourrais un jour remporter une somme aussi importante. Aujourd'hui, cette victoire représente pour moi une grande satisfaction et un moment inoubliable », a-t-il confié. Concernant ses projets, Mohamed Diallo entend également investir dans la construction. Pour lui, ce gain représente une occasion de concrétiser une ambition et de poser les bases d'un avenir meilleur. Présidant la cérémonie de remise des chèques, le directeur du Marketing et de la Communication de la LONAGUI, Algassimou Bah, a apporté des précisions sur le fonctionnement du jeu ayant permis aux deux parieurs de remporter cette somme. Il a notamment expliqué que le jeu « Extra 7-5 numéros » consiste à trouver cinq numéros parmi les sept numéros tirés. « Extra 7-5 numéros, c'est un jeu de l'Auto-Fortune. Il suffit d'avoir 5 numéros sur les 7 numéros tirés. Mais c'est un choix. Tu viens, tu dis au revendeur : « Je vais jouer à Extra 7-5 numéros. » La combinaison coûte 2 000 francs guinéens le ticket. Donc, quand tu mises sur les 7 numéros tirés, si tu prends 5 numéros et que les 5 numéros sortent en ordre ou en désordre, tu gagnes 300 millions de francs guinéens », a-t-il expliqué. Selon lui, l'Auto-Fortune propose quotidiennement douze tirages, auxquels s'ajoute un tirage du Jackpot milliardaire, soit treize tirages au total. Ces opérations se déroulent toutes les heures, de 9 heures à 21 heures, offrant ainsi plusieurs occasions de participer aux différents jeux. Il a également insisté sur la rapidité du processus de paiement des gains, qu'il présente comme un élément important dans le renforcement de la confiance entre la LONAGUI et ses parieurs. À titre d'exemple, il a indiqué que l'un des deux bénéficiaires avait remporté son gain la veille de la cérémonie et avait déjà reçu son chèque avant 13 heures ce lundi. « Un parieur qui gagne tout de suite là, à 13h, 14h, d'ici 17h à la fin de l'heure, même si c'est 1 milliard, il va être payé », a-t-il assuré. Algassimou Bah a, par ailleurs, souligné l'importance accordée par la direction générale au règlement des gains des parieurs. Il a notamment évoqué l'engagement du directeur général, Mohamed Baba Sylla, à faciliter la signature des chèques afin que les bénéficiaires puissent entrer rapidement en possession de leur argent. « La seule chose, là où notre directeur général, Mohamed Baba Sylla, ne nous retarde pas dans cette société, c'est la signature du chèque d'un gagnant. Même s'il est en réunion, l'assistant fait rentrer le portefeuille, il signe, il ne badine pas avec ça », a-t-il affirmé. Youssouf Keita L’article LONAGUI : deux parieurs remportent chacun 300 millions GNF et reçoivent officiellement leurs chèques en moins de 24 heures est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: ShaQ Express unveils advisory board to strengthen growth agenda
items.description: Ghanaian logistics company ShaQ Express has appointed seasoned entrepreneur and business advisor, Ms Leah Nduati as chairman of its Advisory Board, as the company seeks to strengthen corporate governance and support the next phase of its growth. Ms Nduati will lead the board, which comprises Charles N. Armah, Felix Nana Osei, Beatrice Bota and Michael Kwabena Acolatse – all seasoned professionals drawn from various sectors – in guiding the budding business to entrench its growth and serve customers better. Members of the committee were unveiled on Monday in a press statement. They will advise the company’s directors and management on corporate strategy and governance, financial management, legal and regulatory affairs, digital financial services and commercial expansion, the statement said. The board will meet quarterly, and members will serve two-year terms, it added. Profiles Ms Nduati is the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Yoga Experiences Africa (YEA) and has more than 15 years of executive and advisory experience building and scaling organisations across African markets. She co-founded The Board Harbor Foundation, a United States nonprofit that prepared founders to build investor ready boards, built ALX Ventures’ accelerator from 10 to 400 companies across eight countries, and led GrowthAfrica’s market entry into Ghana. Mr Armah is a senior Director of Financial Planning and Analysis at Last Mile Health. He previously served as Director of Finance, IT and Procurement for Ghana and Sierra Leone at MSI Reproductive Choices. Mr Armah began his career leading audit teams at PricewaterhouseCoopers. He is a Fellow of the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants. Mr Osei is a Senior Associate at Beacon Law Consult in Accra, where he advises corporate clients on compliance, data protection, governance and commercial agreements. He was called to the Ghana Bar in 2012 and holds an LLM in International Commercial Law from the University of Salford. Ms Bota is a governance, risk and compliance professional with more than a decade of experience in digital financial services and payments regulation. She led the development of BrijX, a currency swap solution approved in the Bank of Ghana regulatory sandbox, and was named Fintech Personality of the Year 2024 (Female). Mr Acolatse is a digital finance professional with more than 15 years of experience building financial services for underserved markets across Africa. He is Commercial Lead, Trade at Nsano and previously led Brassica Pay through Bank of Ghana licensing as its Chief Commercial Officer. He has also held senior roles at BIMA Ghana, PEG Africa and Millicom (Tigo Cash). Tapping experience Speaking on the appointments, the Director and General Manager of ShaQ Express, Madam Rhoda Folie, said the Board gives the company independent counsel from people who have built, financed and governed organisations across Africa. “Their judgement on governance, finance, regulation and commercial growth will sharpen the decisions we take as we expand our services to businesses and customers across Ghana,” she said. Ms Nduati commended ShaQ Express successfully building a logistics operation that serves businesses across Ghana. She said the Advisory Board would help management strengthen governance, prepare the company for its next stage of growth and open new markets, pledging to work hard with the members to uplift the company ShaQ Express was founded in 2020 and operates delivery services nationwide from nine regional branches, using a mixed fleet of electric and conventional motorbikes. Its services include last-mile delivery, fulfilment and warehousing, and intercity and bulk delivery.

items.title: Kpélé/techniques de transformation du maïs jaune en couscous : Trente femmes formées à Adeta
items.description: Adeta, 2 nov. (ATOP) – Trente femmes des sociétés coopératives (SCOOPS) des préfectures d’Anié, Agou, Amou, Danyi, Kloto, Wawa et de Kpélé ont été formées sur les techniques de transformation du maïs jaune en couscous et sa mise en sachet du 27 au 30 octobre à Adeta. Cette initiative est portée par la Chambre régionale d’agriculture des Plateaux avec l’appui financier du Fonds national d’apprentissage, de formation et de perfectionnement professionnels (FNAFPP). La formation est assurée par le Centre agro-pastorale pour la promotion des entreprises (CAPE). Elle vise à renforcer les compétences des participantes sur les techniques de transformation du maïs jaune en couscous et sa mise en sachet. Il est aussi question de développer les compétences permettant de transformer les matières premières agricoles en produits de qualité, susceptibles de répondre aux besoins des consommateurs et aux exigences du marché. Les bénéficiaires ont acquis des connaissances portant sur le processus de transformation du maïs jaune en couscous notamment le choix et la sélection du maïs ; les méthodes de vannage, de tri à main, de lavage, de décorticage ; les techniques de mouture et de pétrissage. Ils ont été également outillés sur les techniques de roulage, de tamisage, de pré- cuisson, de broyage, de séchage, de conservation et de mise en sachet. Le chef d’antenne régional du FNAFPP des Plateaux, Bomboma Nam a indiqué que la transformation du maïs jaune en couscous constitue une opportunité de création de valeur ajoutée et d’amélioration des revenus des bénéficiaires. « La fin de cette formation marque le début d’une nouvelle étape, celle de la mise en pratique des connaissances acquises. Je vous encourage donc à mettre en œuvre au sein de votre coopérative respective, les compétences développées au cours de cette formation. Faites de la qualité, de l’hygiène et de l’innovation et de rigueur vos principes directeurs”, a-t-il conseillé. Le président de la chambre régionale d’agriculture des Plateaux, Koussodou Kofi a exprimé sa gratitude au président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé pour sa politique de valorisation des produits agricoles locaux par leur transformation pour tirer pleinement profit de ces ressources. ATOP/SKD/MD/KYA

items.title: NDC Western Region: George Dadzie Junior tipped for Regional Secretary role
items.description: As the National Democratic Congress (NDC) prepares for its upcoming Western Regional elections, George Dadzie Junior is being presented as a strong candidate to succeed Joseph Nelson as the party’s Regional Secretary following his exit from the position to serve as Western Regional Minister. For some party delegates and supporters, the next Regional Secretary must be more than an administrator. They say the position requires a unifying figure who understands collective leadership, organisational discipline and inclusive party development. Against this background, George Dadzie Junior’s candidature is being promoted as an opportunity to build a stronger, more coordinated and electorally competitive NDC in the Western Region. According to Emmanuel Yirenkyi, an ardent party member, the demands of the office require someone capable of bringing different interests together while strengthening the party’s structures at all levels. “The task ahead requires a bridge-builder, an organiser, a communicator and a committed party man. George Dadzie Junior is presenting himself as that candidate, with a vision to serve the party, strengthen its structures and work with every stakeholder towards a common political objective: a stronger NDC and sustained electoral success in the Western Region,” he said in an interview. Mr Yirenkyi said delegates were increasingly considering Mr Dadzie as a credible candidate, citing his experience, charisma, dedication and commitment to the party’s development. He identified six key areas underpinning the candidate’s proposed leadership agenda: unity and internal cohesion; experience and institutional knowledge; hard work and accessibility; youth empowerment and capacity development; women’s empowerment and inclusive leadership; and strategic communication, grassroots mobilisation and electoral success. Unity and internal cohesion Mr Yirenkyi said one of the most important qualities required of the next Regional Secretary was the ability to unite party members across constituencies, branches and competing political interests. He argued that the NDC’s strength depended on its collective identity and shared commitment to the party’s ideals, adding that internal divisions could undermine its electoral fortunes. According to him, Mr Dadzie’s leadership vision places unity above personal interests and seeks to build bridges between competing factions, reconcile differences and create an environment in which every member feels valued and respected. “For him, the NDC must remain one formidable political family, where cooperation and mutual respect take precedence over factional considerations,” he said. Experience and institutional knowledge Mr Yirenkyi also identified experience and an understanding of the party’s organisational structures as essential requirements for the position. He noted that the office of Regional Secretary involved significant administrative and political responsibilities, including internal coordination, political mobilisation and the effective management of the regional secretariat. He said Mr Dadzie’s involvement in party activities had given him an understanding of the NDC’s organisational dynamics, providing a foundation for coordination, strategic decision-making and the implementation of policies to strengthen the party. “Delegates require a secretary who will not spend valuable time learning the responsibilities of the office but will demonstrate readiness to deliver from the beginning,” he stressed. Hard work, commitment and accessibility On the demands of the position, Mr Yirenkyi said the Regional Secretary’s role went beyond ceremonial responsibilities and required availability, sacrifice and a willingness to work beyond conventional office hours. He described Mr Dadzie’s political appeal as being associated with hard work, dedication and active participation in party activities. He argued that the next Regional Secretary must maintain close contact with constituency executives, branch officers, grassroots organisers, electoral area coordinators and ordinary party members. According to him, Mr Dadzie’s proposed approach is to establish an active regional secretariat that responds promptly to members’ concerns and provides the administrative and organisational support needed by party structures. He added that effective leadership required practical engagement with members rather than distant administration. Youth empowerment and capacity development Mr Yirenkyi said the future strength of the NDC in the Western Region would depend partly on its ability to empower young people and prepare them for greater responsibilities within the party. He argued that young people should not be mobilised only during election campaigns but should also be given meaningful opportunities to participate in decision-making, leadership development and party administration. He said Mr Dadzie’s vision included promoting skills development, mentorship, political education and opportunities for emerging young leaders. “By investing in the next generation of political leaders, he believes the party can build a sustainable organisational structure capable of responding to changing political realities and securing the confidence of younger voters,” he said. Women’s empowerment and inclusive leadership The NDC stalwart also highlighted the importance of women’s participation in the party’s leadership and organisational activities. He described women as an indispensable part of the party’s political strength, citing their contributions to grassroots mobilisation, campaign organisation, community engagement and electoral success. He said Mr Dadzie’s leadership agenda recognised the need to create more opportunities for women to occupy leadership positions and contribute meaningfully to party decision-making. According to him, the candidate envisages an inclusive political environment in which women, young people, experienced party stalwarts and grassroots members have opportunities to contribute to the party’s development. “An effective Regional Secretary must be a unifying administrator who gives every segment of the party a sense of belonging,” he said. Strategic communication, grassroots mobilisation and electoral success Mr Yirenkyi said the effectiveness of a Regional Secretary should ultimately be measured by the strength of the party’s organisation and its ability to translate political support into electoral victories. He noted that effective communication, grassroots mobilisation, information management and continuous engagement with constituency and branch executives were critical to achieving that objective. He said Mr Dadzie’s vision included strengthening communication between the regional secretariat and constituency structures to ensure that information flowed efficiently and party members remained informed, motivated and politically active. He further highlighted strategic planning, delegate engagement and continuous political education as important tools for sustaining the NDC’s electoral strength in the Western Region. As the party approaches the regional elections, Mr Yirenkyi believes these six thematic areas provide a compelling basis for Mr Dadzie’s candidature. He maintains that a Regional Secretary who combines organisational experience with accessibility, inclusiveness and strategic communication would be well positioned to strengthen internal cohesion and prepare the party for future electoral contests.

items.title: Les midterms, c’est quoi | Concepts
items.description: Tous les quatre ans, les Américains élisent leur président. Deux ans plus tard viennent les midterms, les élections de mi-mandat, essentielles à leur démocratie. Lors de ces élections de mi-mandat, les Américains ne votent pas pour leur président. Ils renouvellent l’ensemble de la Chambre des représentants, un tiers du Sénat, et désignent aussi des gouverneurs et des élus locaux. Les midterms peuvent alors bouleverser les rapports de force à Washington. Romuald Sciora, chercheur associé à l’IRIS où il dirige l’Observatoire politique et géostratégique des États-Unis, revient sur son rôle. L’article Les midterms, c'est quoi | Concepts est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Ghana must turn scientific research into practical industrial solutions – CSIR-IIR director
items.description: The new Director of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research’s Institute of Industrial Research (CSIR-IIR), Dr William Owusu Oduro, has called for a shift towards industry-focused scientific research, warning that innovations that fail to address manufacturers’ practical needs could undermine Ghana’s industrial ambitions. He says research institutions must prioritise technologies that help local businesses improve production, reduce costs and compete with imported products. Delivering his inaugural address, Dr Oduro proposed an industry immersion programme that would place technical staff directly within manufacturing companies to identify operational challenges and develop practical solutions. He said the initiative would help researchers better understand the needs of businesses and produce technologies that could be adopted and commercialised, rather than remaining at the prototype stage. Dr Oduro cited trade figures for January to August 2026, which he said showed that China exported goods worth US$10.2 billion to Ghana, an increase of about 23 per cent compared with the same period in 2025. Ghana, in contrast, exported goods worth US$1.3 billion to China, representing a decline from previous years. He said the imbalance was also reflected in the composition of trade between the two countries, with China’s exports consisting largely of finished, high-value products, while Ghana’s exports were dominated by petroleum and manganese. According to him, the figures underscore the need for Ghana to strengthen its manufacturing capacity and develop local technologies that can support more efficient production. Private sector urged to invest in research Dr Oduro also identified inadequate funding as a major constraint facing research institutions, arguing that greater private-sector investment would be necessary to sustain innovation and ensure research delivers commercial value. “The money we need for research is with the private sector,” he said. He explained that businesses were more likely to invest in research when its outcomes could improve profitability, reduce operational costs or address specific production challenges. He said CSIR-IIR must therefore align its research agenda with industry needs and demonstrate the commercial value of its innovations to attract investment and build sustainable partnerships. Dr Oduro believes stronger collaboration between researchers and manufacturers would help bridge the gap between scientific innovation and industrial application, making research a more active contributor to Ghana’s economic transformation.

items.title: GPHA Fire and Safety, LCB Worldwide Ghana crowned champions of 2026 LCB corporate games
items.description: The Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) Fire and Safety team and LCB Worldwide Ghana football team have emerged champions of the 2026 LCB Corporate Games in the Tema and Accra zones respectively, following weeks of competitive football action. The grand finale of the 5th edition of the competition was held on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at Mexico Park, Community 2, Tema, bringing together participating companies from the ports and shipping industry and other sectors. In the Tema Zone final, GPHA Fire and Safety secured a narrow 1-0 victory over the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) team to clinch the ultimate title. In another decisive encounter, LCB Worldwide Ghana delivered an impressive performance in the Accra Zone, thrashing the Ghana Immigration Service team 5-0 to emerge champions. The final standings saw LCB Worldwide Ghana finish first in the Accra zone, followed by the Ghana Immigration Service in second place, while Manna team settled for third. In the Tema zone, GPHA Fire and Safety claimed the top spot, with the Ghana National Fire Service finishing as runners-up and Wilmar Africa taking third place. Winners take home cash prizes The victorious teams were rewarded with cash prizes in recognition of their performances. The champions in both zones received GH¢20,000 each, while the first runners-up took home GH¢10,000 each. The second runners-up were also rewarded with GH¢5,000 each. Individual awards were presented to outstanding performers, with the tournament’s top scorer receiving GH¢2,000 and the best goalkeeper taking home GH¢1,000. 16 teams compete in 5th edition A total of 16 teams, comprising eight teams from each zone, participated in this year’s competition, which featured several weeks of exciting football action. The Accra zone participants included the Ghana Union of Traders (GUTA), Ghana Institute of Freight Forwarders (GIFF), LCB Worldwide Ghana, Ghana Immigration Service, Aviance, Mariners, Manna and Conquerors. The Tema zone was represented by Port Hub, GPHA Fire and Safety, Ghana National Fire Service, GPHA Mechanical, Ezeylinks, Wilmar Africa, Tema Metropolitan Assembly (TMA) and Ghana Dock Labour Company Limited (GDLC). LCB eyes expansion of corporate games Speaking to the media on the sidelines of the grand finale, a representative of the Human Resource Department at LCB Worldwide, Solomon Dwamena Aboagye expressed satisfaction with the performance of the participating teams and the overall impact of the competition. He noted that the objectives behind organising the games had consistently been achieved over the years, adding that LCB Worldwide Ghana remained committed to expanding the initiative to attract more corporate organisations. “We are hoping that in the next few years, the participating companies will be more. We are hoping to bring companies from other industries. We are expecting the financial institutions, oil and gas companies and even the educational sector as well,” he said. Mr. Aboagye further disclosed that the competition was fully sponsored by LCB Worldwide Ghana, expressing optimism that the company would continue to mobilise resources to sustain and increase the prize money in subsequent editions. Promoting corporate unity through sports The LCB Worldwide Corporate Games was initiated to foster camaraderie, strengthen professional relationships and promote bonds of friendship among companies, particularly those operating within the ports and shipping industry. Beyond sports, LCB Worldwide Ghana has also established a strong presence through its corporate social responsibility initiatives. The crisis management company has been operating in Ghana since 2017 and has been contracted by the Government of Ghana, through the Ministry of Health, to undertake fumigation and disinfection of cargo at the country’s ports and designated points of entry and exit. As part of its commitment to public health and community development, the company has undertaken fumigation exercises at markets, hospitals, senior high schools and tertiary educational institutions across the country.

items.title: Culture : L’Inde et le Togo célèbrent leurs liens d’amitié à travers Diwali
items.description: Lomé , 2 nov. (ATOP) – L’ambassade de l’Inde au Togo et l’association indienne du Togo ont organisé, le dimanche 1 er novembre, la 4ᵉ édition de l’India Festival « Diwali », une soirée célébrant la richesse du patrimoine indien ainsi que les liens d’amitié et de coopération entre l’Inde et le Togo. Cette manifestation a permis de mettre en lumière la richesse du patrimoine indien à travers ses expressions artistiques, culturelles et traditionnelles. Elle a également illustré le rôle essentiel de la culture comme passerelle entre les peuples et instrument de rapprochement entre les nations. Au-delà des prestations culturelles, le festival a offert un espace d’exposition aux entreprises indiennes et togolaises, qui ont présenté et commercialisé leurs produits. Des sociétés pharmaceutiques indiennes ont, pour leur part, installé un camp médical permettant aux visiteurs de bénéficier gratuitement de plusieurs contrôles de santé. Ces consultations ont porté notamment sur des pathologies comme le diabète, le cholestérol, la tension artérielle ainsi que le contrôle des vitamines. Le ministre du Tourisme, de la Culture et des Arts, Isaac Tchiakpé a souligné l’importance de la culture dans le rapprochement entre les peuples. « A travers la musique, la danse, la gastronomie et les arts, ce festival nous rappelle que la diversité culturelle est une richesse partagée parce qu’elle est notre nature commune. Il nous rappelle que la culture est un trésor et une source de dialogue, de compréhension mutuelle et d’amitié », a-t-il déclaré. Le président de l’association indienne Togo, Sani Vaswani a expliqué que cette manifestation ne vise pas uniquement à rassembler la communauté indienne vivant au Togo, mais également à favoriser les échanges avec les populations togolaises. « Nous organisons ce festival non seulement pour marquer l’événement et réunir notre communauté de la diaspora, qui vit ici au Togo depuis plusieurs décennies, mais aussi pour échanger et partager notre culture, nos traditions et notre mode de vie avec les Togolais », a-t-il souligné. Connue comme la fête des lumières, Diwali symbolise la victoire de la lumière sur les ténèbres et du bien sur le mal. Elle est célébrée à travers des rites séculaires, l’illumination de lampes traditionnelles et un magnifique déploiement de couleurs. L’ambassadeur de l’Inde au Togo, Shri Sayed Razi Haider Fahmi a pris part à cet événement. ATOP/MD/MG

items.title: Carrick shrugs off Man Utd sack talk ahead of Roma match
items.description: Michael Carrick brushed off suggestions he has just two games left as Manchester United boss as he prepares his underperforming side for Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Roma. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford is increasingly precarious following Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, which extended United’s winless run in all competitions to nine games — they last had a longer such sequence in 1984. Former United and England midfielder Carrick was asked at his pre-match press conference on Monday whether he felt he had just two games remaining at the helm — against Roma and Aston Villa. The Villa match on Sunday comes just before an international break, potentially giving the United hierarchy an opportunity to make a managerial change. “No, not at all,” said the 45-year-old, in his first full season in charge. “If you look into the future, you never know what’s going to happen. “I don’t know what’s going to happen. That doesn’t change the way I feel, how we’re preparing for the game tomorrow. “I’m actually really looking forward to the game, can’t wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I’m crazy with the results we’ve had and what’s going on, but I genuinely can’t wait.” Carrick also said he had “no concerns” over the commitment of out-of-form Argentine centre-back Lisandro Martinez, who was sent off in United’s defeat at Stamford Bridge. The defender had previously criticised club chiefs over a lack of investment in the squad. “Things happen in football, sometimes you do things, sometimes you make decisions, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but the commitment is not an issue for sure,” said Carrick. – Dressing-room mood – The United head coach insisted the dressing room was in “a good place” despite the club’s terrible start to the season. “Perception is a funny thing. You can make things look all sorts of different ways and think about all sorts of different things,” he said. “I’ve said it before, the commitment of the players to the club, to me, to each other, I don’t question that at all. We need to play better, we can make better decisions, but commitment is not a thing at all.” United are just one place above the Premier League relegation zone after taking a mere seven points from their nine matches so far this season. And they are 20th in the Champions League table following a dismal 4-1 defeat away at Como last month. Only the top 24 teams will progress beyond the league phase. But midfielder Kobbie Mainoo, sitting alongside Carrick at Monday’s press conference, said United could turn things around. “We’ve not had the results we’ve wanted,” said the 21-year-old. “But we need to look forward now. There’s big, big games ahead and I feel like we’re one win away from changing that.” Carrick has fond memories of facing Roma as a member of Alex Ferguson’s team, scoring twice in United’s 7-1 quarter-final second-leg triumph in the Champions League in 2007. “It was a magical night, I have to say,” he recalled. “It was one of the best nights, one of the best games, one of the best atmospheres I’ve been fortunate enough to witness. “The fact that I scored a couple and that was very unusual gives me great memories, but it was more the emotion of the night. I have to say, it was a special one.” The post Carrick shrugs off Man Utd sack talk ahead of Roma match appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Jeux Olympiques 2036 : Sept pays intéressés pour l’organisation
items.description: Au total, sept pays ont confirmé leur intérêt d’accueillir les Jeux Olympiques de 2036. Il s’agit, selon un communiqué du Comité International Olympique (CIO) rendu public lundi, de l’Afrique du Sud, de l’Allemagne, de la Hongrie, de l’Inde, du Qatar, de la République de Corée et du Türkiye. Le Comité International Olympique (CIO) a reconfirmé la liste des parties intéressées ayant manifesté leur souhait d'accueillir les Jeux Olympiques de 2036. Dans le cadre de la transparence du processus de sélection de l'hôte, tel qu'approuvé par la Session de l'institution olympique en juin, les noms de ces parties intéressées ont été rendus publics par le CIO le 6 octobre. « Les sept CNO qui seront pris en considération par le CIO en tant qu'hôtes potentiels à l'organisation des Jeux Olympiques de 2036 sont, dans l'ordre alphabétique : Afrique du Sud, Allemagne, Hongrie, Inde, Qatar, République de Corée et Türkiye », informe le CIO dans un communiqué rendu public le lundi 2 novembre 2026. A lire aussi : JOJ Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal s’incline face à l’Australie en rugby féminin Le CIO avait également fixé une date limite pour que d'autres Comités Nationaux Olympiques (CNO) puissent entamer des discussions concernant l'édition de 2036. Cette période est désormais terminée, et aucune autre partie intéressée ne s'est manifestée. D’après la présidente de la commission de futur hôte pour les Jeux de l'Olympiade et membre du CIO, Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović, ce sera la première édition des Jeux Olympiques dont l'organisation sera attribuée dans le cadre des changements apportés par le processus « Fit for the Future ». « Le vif intérêt suscité par l'accueil des Jeux Olympiques de 2036 montre que les pays du monde entier reconnaissent la valeur sociale et économique durable que les Jeux peuvent apporter aux communautés locales. Nous continuerons à travailler en étroite collaboration avec les sept parties intéressées afin de les aider à développer leurs projets », a-t-il dit. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Adrian Hamilton-Manns appointed new PIA chief executive officer
items.description: The board of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) on Monday announced the appointment of Adrian Hamilton-Manns as its chief executive officer (CEO). In a press release, PIA said Hamilton-Manns “brings a wealth of leadership and strategic experience within the global aviation sector”, adding that his appointment “marks a pivotal chapter” in the airline’s ongoing transformation. It said that he had managed three airlines as CEO and was considered a “world expert” in transforming and reviving airlines, with over 30 years of experience. “As Hamilton-Manns assumes the role of CEO, the consortium and the entire management board extend their deepest gratitude to the outgoing CEO, Air Vice Marshal (AVM) Amir Hayat, for his outstanding service and dedication to this vital national role,” the statement said. It added that over his four-and-a-half-year tenure, Hayat’s leadership was “instrumental in navigating the airline through significant industry challenges”. “His relentless efforts were central to initiating comprehensive structural reforms, optimising operational efficiencies and successfully preparing the airline for its highly anticipated privatisation phase,” it said. “The foundation he has laid will be critical to the carrier’s future commercial viability and success,” it added. The statement said that with Hamilton-Manns at the helm, PIA was confident that his extensive industry expertise would accelerate strategic objectives, elevate service standards and drive sustainable profitability in this new era. According to Forbes Middle East , Hamilton-Manns was previously the CEO of Oman’s SalamAir and Kazakhstan-based FlyArystan. He also held roles at South African Airways and Virgin Australia. The national flag carrier was privatised in December last year through an auction. A consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited had won the auction for 75 per cent shares of PIA in December last year, making a winning bid of Rs135 billion. The Arif Habib-led consortium, which took charge in June this year, had vowed to transform the loss-making airline through operational restructuring, fleet expansion, and improved customer service. On Sunday, the carrier’s first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner , acquired on lease last month, arrived in Islamabad from London as flight PK786. A PIA spokesperson said that the carrier was the first Pakistani airline to have added a Boeing 787-9 to its fleet.

items.title: Miner dies in pit collapse in Plateau
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — A 35-year-old miner, identified as Ibrahim Jabir, has died following the collapse of a mining pit at Asaradan village in Jos East Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 12:10 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, 2026, trapping the miner in the collapsed pit. A resident of Jos East, Peter Ajik, who confirmed the incident to newsmen in Jos on Monday, said Jabir died at the scene. “The victim, Ibrahim Jabir, died in the incident. The incident happened around 12:10 a.m. when the mining pit collapsed,” Ajik said. He described the incident as another reminder of the dangers associated with mining activities, particularly where adequate safety measures are not observed. Ajik urged miners to take safety precautions seriously and called on relevant authorities to intensify monitoring of mining activities in the area. He also said security operatives responded to a distress call following the collapse. “We are appealing to the relevant authorities to intensify monitoring of mining activities in the area and ensure that safety measures are strictly observed to prevent further loss of lives,” he said. Efforts to reach security operatives for further details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Miner dies in pit collapse in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Une autre première mondiale à l’actif d’Essaouira où dialoguent Gnaoua et soufisme judeo-musulman
items.description: La 21e édition du Festival des Andalousies Atlantiques a pris fin, samedi soir à Essaouira, sur les rythmes d'une première musicale inédite entre la Maalma Hind Ennaira et le groupe HaPiyut Ensemble, qui ont fait vibrer le public au son du Hajjoujj et des chants les plus purs de l’école du soufisme judéo-marocain. Rehaussée par la présence notamment du Conseiller du Roi et Président Fondateur de l'Association Essaouira-Mogador, André Azoulay, ainsi que d'éminentes personnalités marocaines et étrangères des sphères diplomatique, culturelle et artistique, cette soirée, sans doute l'un des temps forts de cette édition, a donné vie et réalité à un projet porté depuis plusieurs années par les organisateurs du festival, qui souhaitaient voir un jour les mélodies gnaoua et les poèmes du piyut marocain se rejoindre sur une même scène, pour célébrer deux traditions profondément enracinées dans l'histoire culturelle du Royaume. Esquissée en 2022 à Dar Souiri, cette initiative a pris une nouvelle dimension à travers un travail musical mené par HaPiyut Ensemble, une formation musicale intergénérationnelle composée de 18 artistes qui se consacrent à la préservation et à la transmission du piyout, l'art de la poésie liturgique chantée profondément ancré dans le patrimoine juif marocain. Pour préparer cette collaboration, les musiciens gnaoua ont partagé leur répertoire avec HaPiyut Ensemble, qui s'est appuyé sur leurs mélodies et leurs rythmes pour les associer à des textes tirés de « Yaguel Yaakov », un recueil de piyoutim écrits au Maroc par la famille Abihssira. Le résultat a donné lieu à un concert des plus raffinés, où près d'une heure et demi durant, les rythmes gnaoua portés par la voix puissante de Hind Ennaira se sont mêlés aux chants de HaPiyut Ensemble, dans un échange musical qui n'a rien effacé des particularités de chaque tradition, incarnant avec brio la richesse des expressions musicales marocaines et témoignant de leur capacité à se renouveler au contact les unes des autres. Dans une déclaration à la presse à l'issue du concert, Hind Ennaira s'est dite heureuse et fière de participer pour la 2e fois au Festival des Andalousies Atlantiques, se réjouissant de clôturer, en tant qu'artiste souirie, cette manifestation culturelle qui a su se tailler, depuis 21 ans, une place parmi les manifestations les plus prestigieuses à l'échelle mondiale. Mettant en avant le caractère singulier de cette collaboration avec HaPiyut Ensemble, qui lui permet d'explorer de nouvelles sonorités tout en restant fidèle à ses racines musicales, elle a également évoqué ses précédentes expériences de fusion, notamment avec l'orchestre andalou d'Amsterdam, tout en expliquant que ces collaborations lui avaient permis de mesurer davantage les possibilités offertes par la musique gnaoua, capable, selon elle, de se mêler à différents genres musicaux. De leur côté, Avraham Cohen et Yair Harel, membres de HaPiyut Ensemble, se sont dits particulièrement heureux de présenter cette création à Essaouira, qu'ils ont qualifiée de capitale mondiale de la musique gnaoua, saluant « le caractère inédit de cette collaboration, fruit d'un travail musical de longue haleine visant à rapprocher les chants du piyut marocain et les rythmes gnaoua dans une même interprétation ». « Cette rencontre musicale porte également un message de paix et de rapprochement entre les peuples », ont-ils relevé, exprimant le souhait de voir cette création voyager sur d'autres scènes à travers le monde en se disant « convaincus que la musique peut rapprocher les cœurs, susciter l'inspiration et ouvrir de nouveaux espaces de rencontre ». La soirée de clôture a aussi été marquée par la prestation de la danseuse et chorégraphe espagnole Olga Pericet, qui s'est produite pour la première fois au Festival des Andalousies Atlantiques. Figure majeure du flamenco contemporain, cette artiste a présenté « Perspectiva de un baile sonoro », une création qui revisite le flamenco traditionnel avec une touche personnelle, avant de partager la scène avec Hamid Ajbar, artiste marocain internationalement reconnu pour son travail de préservation et de fusion de la musique arabo-andalouse et du flamenco. Approchée par la MAP, Olga Pericet s'est dite honorée de prendre part à ce grand Festival, saluant l'occasion de partager la scène avec les musiciens marocains. « Cette rencontre dépasse le cadre d'une simple prestation commune, elle met en vedette la dimension spirituelle et les liens profonds de cette union entre les traditions musicales marocaine et andalouse », a-t-elle poursuivi. Plus tôt dans la journée, Dar Souiri avait accueilli le rendez-vous « Marhba Blli Ja Andna », qui a réuni Nouhaila El Kalai, avec le Chaâbi Fassi, Anass Belhachemi, représentant de la Taqtoqa Jabalia, et Hicham Dinar, autour du répertoire musical des Juifs marocains. Le programme de cette dernière journée du festival s'est poursuivi avec Mohamed Aaboud, qui a proposé un répertoire mêlant musique andalouse, « mawwals », chants de zaouïas et chansons populaires du Nord du Maroc, offrant aux mélomanes un nouvel aperçu des différentes facettes du patrimoine musical marocain. Initiée par l'Association Essaouira-Mogador, cette 21e édition du Festival des Andalousies Atlantiques, placée sous le thème « Alif x Alef : deux lettres, une même histoire », a une nouvelle fois tenu toutes ses promesses, en fédérant des artistes de différents horizons autour de traditions musicales qui témoignent de la richesse et de la diversité du patrimoine culturel marocain, tout en consacrant la place d'Essaouira comme un espace privilégié de rencontre, de dialogue et de coexistence entre les cultures. Au fil des concerts et des rencontres, le Festival a poursuivi sa mission de faire vivre à Essaouira les valeurs d'ouverture, de tolérance et de coexistence qui font son ADN. items.title: Democrats, Trump hold final rallies before midterm elections
items.description: Donald Trump and his Republican Party will make last-gasp pitches to US midterm voters Monday to hold back a predicted Democrat wave that could sweep Congress and impose tight political constraints on the president for the first time in two years. For his closing arguments, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president’s controversial drive to redevelop the US capital. “We’re going to win,” he said on Sunday. Democrats, meanwhile, prepared a round of final rallies — including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas — which will cap a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness. Polls are largely in their favor, showing that Democrats are poised to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate. Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues. The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into a lame-duck period, with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran, and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington. But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats are wary about predictions of victory. “Nauseously optimistic,” Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood. – Scorched earth – Democrats are also facing late internal divisions, with left-wing candidates clashing at times with the party’s establishment. In a startling display of infighting on Sunday, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens in Michigan endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed in her state’s key Senate race. Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, struggled to explain her decision in an interview with CNN. Trump’s Republicans have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding El-Sayed, who is Muslim, as a terrorist. Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are “extreme and dangerous radicals” who will “steal your wealth” and let in migrants to “ransack, rape and plunder.” But polls show Americans souring on Trump’s wrecking-ball act. While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air. Only a third of the Senate’s 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favorable to Democrats. To win the upper chamber, Democrats must flip seats in states the president carried by double digits two years before. This has only happened five times in midterm elections since 1990. In its last pre-election day projection, forecaster Decision Desk HQ had the Senate flipping to 52-48 in favor of the Democrats, and the party notching a comfortable 241-194 margin in the House. And the final New York Times/Siena poll released Sunday evening showed Democratic candidates leading in all seven seats viewed as most competitive, though five remained within the margin of error. A Democratic Senate would be able to shut down Trump’s lifetime appointments to courts — including the Supreme Court. While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country. The midterms have seen about $11 billion spent on advertising, with large chunks coming from individual mega-donors. Elon Musk, a close Trump ally who led the so-called DOGE effort in dismantling entire government departments, has given a staggering nearly half-billion dollars to help get Republicans elected. items.title: PWREP challenges prosecution to prove GH¢49.1m in Adu-Boahene trial was public money
items.description: The Parties Without Representation in Parliament (PWREP) has challenged the prosecution in the trial of former National Signals Bureau Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene to establish that the GH¢49.1 million at the centre of the case was public money. The group argues that the State must prove the ownership and source of the disputed funds rather than rely solely on evidence that money was transferred between bank accounts. According to PWREP, the prosecution must demonstrate whether the funds formed part of an approved government allocation or were released through the government’s financial management system. It maintains that establishing the public ownership of the money is central to proving the alleged theft and financial loss to the State. Speaking on behalf of the group, the General Secretary of the Ghana Union Movement (GUM), Anthony Gold Ahinful, said the prosecution must address the source and ownership of the funds as part of its case. “The central question before the court is not merely whether funds moved between bank accounts,” he said. He added that the prosecution must establish “the alleged public character and ownership of the funds”, alongside the alleged lack of authority for the transactions and the criminal intent behind them. PWREP argues that these issues must be resolved before the accused persons can be held criminally responsible. The group insists that the prosecution must establish the essential elements of the allegations with evidence, rather than assume that the movement of funds between accounts is sufficient to prove the offences.
