items.title: 2027: Obi couldn’t fix Anambra; Atiku will return to Dubai after election — Oshiomhole
items.description: Sekinat Osundiji Senator Adams Oshiomhole has criticised former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, questioning their capacity to lead Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Oshiomhole said Obi failed to address Anambra State’s challenges during his eight years as governor, while predicting that Atiku would return to Dubai after losing the presidential election. The former Edo State governor made the remarks during an All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally in Cross River State, where he urged residents to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Questioning Obi’s promise to govern Nigeria for only four years, Oshiomhole said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDCa) had not demonstrated the capacity to deliver within that period. “If Peter Obi could not fix Anambra State in eight years, how can he look you korokoro in the eye and say he will do it in four years?” he asked. He also took a swipe at Atiku, accusing the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of spending much of his time outside the country and returning to Nigeria during election periods. “Atiku, who lives in Dubai, only comes home at the eve of every election. When he loses this one, as he will lose, in January or by February, Atiku will be back in Dubai,” he said. Oshiomhole, however, used the campaign to highlight what he described as the achievements of the Tinubu administration, particularly in Cross River State. He said the state’s recognition as an oil-producing state following the resolution of its non-littoral status would increase revenue accruing to the state and improve its economic prospects. On education, the senator said the Federal Government’s student loan scheme had provided opportunities for young people whose parents could not afford their school fees. He described Tinubu as a leader who prioritises access to education, arguing that students should not be denied opportunities because of their parents’ financial circumstances. Oshiomhole also pointed to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road project, saying its completion would bring economic opportunities and development to Cross River State. The senator also defended the Tinubu administration’s economic policies, particularly the abolition of multiple exchange rates. He argued that the previous system created different exchange rates for people based on their connections, adding that the current arrangement had established a uniform exchange rate across the country. According to Oshiomhole, implementing the policies required courage and visionary leadership. He urged Cross River residents to reject the opposition parties, insisting that the APC had established a strong political presence in the state. “Today, tomorrow, and forever, I believe APC has come to stay in Cross River, and together we will advance the growth and development of Nigeria,” he said. items.title: Le ministre de l’intérieur estime que les prestations de la société Chargée de la propreté de Nouakchott « en deçà des attentes »
items.description: Le ministre de l'Intérieur, de la Décentralisation et du Développement local, Mokhtar Ould Ahmed Bouceif, a déclaré que les prestations de la société « ARMA », chargée de la propreté de la ville de Nouakchott, n'étaient pas à la hauteur des attentes, soulignant la nécessité de remédier aux dysfonctionnements constatés et d'améliorer le niveau de respect des engagements contractuels, dans le délai accordé à la société, soit d'ici la fin du mois de décembre prochain. Lors d’une réunion au siège du ministère, consacrée à l’évaluation de la situation en matière de propreté dans la capitale et à l’examen des performances de la société, le ministre a expliqué que la persistance de la présence de déchets dans plusieurs quartiers et rues de Nouakchott reflétait des lacunes dans l’exécution du contrat, malgré les efforts déployés par les autorités administratives, les secteurs gouvernementaux et les partenaires dans le cadre des campagnes de nettoyage. Ould Bouceif a souligné que la responsabilité du secteur en matière de supervision de la propreté impose de mobiliser toutes les ressources disponibles, affirmant que l’objectif principal est d’assurer la propreté de la capitale, que ce soit en corrigeant les performances de la société actuelle ou en recourant à d’autres solutions garantissant la continuité du service. Il a indiqué que le délai accordé à la société « Arma » jusqu’à la fin du mois de décembre prochain devrait constituer une occasion de remédier aux lacunes, tout en appelant à entamer l’étude des options alternatives sans attendre l’expiration de ce délai, afin d’éviter tout retard pouvant résulter des procédures de passation de marché avec un autre prestataire. Dans ce contexte, le ministre a ordonné la mise en œuvre d’une série de mesures, parmi lesquelles l’élaboration d’un plan d’évacuation des déchets accumulés dans les décharges provisoires, la mise en service de toutes les décharges disponibles au lieu de se limiter à une seule, ainsi que l’étude de la situation du centre d’enfouissement de Tifirit et l’évaluation de son état de préparation. Il a également décidé de mettre les moyens logistiques et les équipements de l’entreprise, à compter du lundi 2 novembre, à la disposition des trois walis de Nouakchott, afin de renforcer la coordination et les interventions sur le terrain dans le domaine de la propreté. Le ministre a demandé aux walis de présenter des propositions concrètes concernant des solutions adéquates à même de résoudre la crise de la propreté de façon permanente étant entendu que le résultat des interventions et des propositions sera présenté lors d’une réunion d’évaluation prévue dimanche 8 novembre 2026.

items.title: Minurso : députés et conseillers unanimes à tourner la page
items.description: Lors de la séance commune des deux Chambres, plusieurs formations politiques ont pris la parole sur la non-reconduction de la mission onusienne, réaffirmant leur mobilisation derrière le Roi Mohammed VI et leur attachement à une clôture définitive du dossier du Sahara marocain. Le Parlement réuni en ses deux Chambres a consacré une séance, ce lundi 2 novembre 2026, aux derniers développements de la cause nationale, au lendemain de la réunion du Conseil de sécurité du 30 octobre et du communiqué du Cabinet Royal qui l’a suivie. Les formations politiques se sont succédé à la tribune pour commenter la non-reconduction du mandat de la Minurso. Toutes interventions convergent sur un point : la fin de cette mission, après 35 ans de présence, doit ouvrir la voie à un règlement définitif. Aini, et au nom du groupe du PAM, Mohamed Sebbari a présenté la non-prorogation de la mission comme un jalon décisif, porteur de significations historiques. À ses yeux, la séance elle-même illustre le ralliement des représentants de la Nation autour du Souverain pour défendre la souveraineté et l’intégrité territoriale du Royaume. Il a également salué les termes du communiqué du Cabinet Royal. Le député a par ailleurs formulé un espoir précis : que cette décision conduise à la clôture définitive du dossier. Cela suppose, a-t-il détaillé, la fin de la présence de la mission sur le terrain, l’arrêt de la saisine du Conseil de sécurité et le retrait de la question de son ordre du jour, ainsi que la fin des réunions périodiques, des rapports du Secrétaire général et des briefings de son Envoyé personnel. Il a souligné l’attachement du Royaume au cessez-le-feu, une approche cohérente, selon lui, avec la vision royale d’un passage de la gestion au changement. Mohamed Sebbari a également retracé le chemin parcouru depuis la résolution 2797 du Conseil de sécurité, qui a fait de l’initiative marocaine d’autonomie la base d’une solution politique définitive, permettant aux habitants des provinces du Sud de gérer leurs affaires au sein d’institutions démocratiques dotées de larges prérogatives, sous la souveraineté du Royaume. La sagesse royale, a-t-il soutenu, a élargi le cercle du soutien international : plus des deux tiers des États membres de l’ONU, dont des membres permanents du Conseil de sécurité et des puissances influentes, appuient désormais l’initiative. Les acquis, a-t-il ajouté, ne sont pas seulement diplomatiques : les provinces du Sud connaissent des mutations dans leurs infrastructures et leurs équipements de base, qui ont renforcé leur intégration économique et sociale et consolidé leur position de porte d’entrée vers le prolongement africain du Royaume. Il a cité le port atlantique de Dakhla et l’autoroute Tiznit-Dakhla. Intervenant au nom du RNI dans les deux Chambres, Mohamed Salem Bahia a placé son propos sur le terrain de la diplomatie. Il a attribué les évolutions en cours à une diplomatie royale posée, qui repose sur la clarté de la vision, la constance de la position, l’accumulation des acquis et la construction d’alliances. Le communiquédu Cabinet royal du 30 octobre traduit, selon lui, un changement qualitatif : on ne se contente plus d’administrer le différend, on œuvre à en modifier les paramètres pour ouvrir des perspectives de règlement définitif. Pour le RNI, a-t-il poursuivi, le moment impose de passer de l’accompagnement des acquis diplomatiques à leur valorisation, et de la mobilisation conjoncturelle à une mobilisation stratégique, afin de convertir ces évolutions en gains politiques et institutionnels durables. Le premier anniversaire de la fête de l’Unité, qui coïncide avec ces développements, confère à l’occasion une charge symbolique particulière. Mohamed Salem Bahia a rappelé que l’unité territoriale n’est pas un slogan mais une réalité enracinée dans l’histoire, fondée sur les liens d’allégeance, les attributs de la souveraineté, les institutions de l’État et la volonté des citoyens. L’engagement du Royaume dans les efforts onusiens procède, a-t-il dit, d’une position de confiance dans ses droits historiques, et la formule « Le Maroc dans son Sahara et le Sahara dans son Maroc » en résume la portée. Au nom du groupe istiqlalien de l’Unité et de l’Égalitarisme à la Chambre des représentants, Rahhal El Mekkaoui y a vu une occasion historique offerte à la communauté internationale de quitter la logique de gestion d’un différend artificiel pour rechercher une solution définitive. La mission, a-t-il argué, était de toute façon dans l’impossibilité d’organiser un référendum comme de dissuader les violations répétées du cessez-le-feu par les milices du polisario. Cette étape doit permettre, selon lui, de rompre avec une situation figée depuis plus de cinq décennies. © Mounir Mehimdate Le chef du groupe istiqlalien a rappelé que l’initiative d’autonomie, présentée par le Maroc en avril 2007, est devenue une référence onusienne et un levier de paix et de stabilité régionales, et que la conviction internationale de son réalisme tient aussi aux réalisations des provinces du Sud et à la participation active de leurs habitants aux scrutins nationaux. Il a repris le chiffre des deux tiers des États membres de l’ONU acquis à l’initiative. Il s’est aussi arrêté sur la situation humanitaire des personnes retenues dans les camps de Tindouf, qui subissent, d’après des rapports internationaux, des conditions difficiles et une exploitation multiforme, estimant que la nouvelle phase devait mettre un terme à cette souffrance. Rahhal El Mekkaoui a renouvelé, au nom du Parti de l’Istiqlal, sa mobilisation derrière le Roi Mohammed VI, assurant que la défense de l’unité territoriale se poursuivrait dans toutes les enceintes et par tous les leviers : politiques, diplomatiques, parlementaires, partisans, civils et populaires. Il a rendu hommage aux sacrifices des Forces Armées Royales, de la Gendarmerie Royale, de la Sûreté nationale, des Forces auxiliaires, de la Protection civile et des composantes de l’administration territoriale, avant de saluer les efforts de la population du Sahara marocain et de ses élus dans la défense de l’intégrité du Royaume. The post Minurso : députés et conseillers unanimes à tourner la page appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ogou/accueil client et communication professionnelle : la COOPEC Ilema renforce les compétences de son personnel
items.description: Atakpamé, 2 nov. (ATOP) – Le personnel de la Coopérative d’épargne et de crédit (COOPEC) ILEMA prend part, du 2 au 8 novembre à Atakpamé, à un atelier de renforcement des capacités sur l’accueil client et la communication professionnelle. L’initiative est organisée par la Coopérative avec le concours financier du Fonds national d’apprentissage, de formation et de perfectionnement professionnels (FNAFPP). Elle ambitionne d’accroître l’expertise des agents sur des thématiques, notamment l’accueil client, la communication professionnelle, les techniques de recouvrement à l’amiable, le montage des dossiers de crédit, ainsi que l’optimisation des performances commerciales et de la gestion de la relation clientèle au sein d’une agence de microfinance. Les participants seront entretenus sur la maîtrise des techniques de collecte et de mobilisation de l’épargne, de la conduite d’actions de prospection ciblée, des stratégies d’adhésion et de fidélisation des membres et clients, ainsi que sur le renforcement de la visibilité et de la notoriété de l’institution sur le marché. Le président du Conseil d’administration de la COOPEC, Dossou Yawo, a exprimé sa gratitude envers le FNAFPP pour son appui financier. Il a exhorté les collaborateurs à faire preuve d’assiduité et d’un vif esprit inquisitif afin de tirer le meilleur parti de cet enseignement. Le maire de la commune Ogou 1, Komlan Kassamada, a salué cette démarche tout en invitant les agents à cultiver l’émulation et le partage d’expériences. Le maire Kassamada a rappelé le rôle pivot de la microfinance dans le tissu économique local par son accompagnement des petites et moyennes entreprises et des ménages. Il a émis le vœu d’une formation fructueuse ancrée dans les réalités du terrain. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence des autorités administratives et locales, ainsi que des représentants du FNAFPP. ATOP/AY/KKT/BA

items.title: SIAO 2026 : à Ouagadougou, les artisans nourrissent de grandes ambitions
items.description: Depuis le 30 octobre, Ouagadougou accueille la 18ᵉ edition du Salon international de l'artisanat (SIAO). Pendant dix jours, plus de 6 000 exposants venus d'une trentaine de pays presentent leurs creations. Pour les artisans, ce rendez-vous constitue une occasion de valoriser leur savoir-faire, de conquerir de nouveaux marches, de realiser des ventes et de nouer des partenariats commerciaux. a peine la ceremonie officielle d'ouverture terminee, les allees du Salon international de l'artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) accueillent deja de nombreux visiteurs. Dans les differents pavillons, les artisans s'activent pour mettre en valeur leurs creations et attirer les premiers clients. Pour certains exposants, le salon represente avant tout une vitrine pour faire connaître leur savoir-faire et promouvoir les produits locaux. Promotion des produits locaux Marceline Ky est creatrice burkinabe specialisee dans le textile. Elle est venue presenter des innovations autour du Faso Dan Fani, notamment des tissus aux motifs inspires de la dentelle industrielle. « C'est une occasion de nous faire connaître, de faire connaître nos produits et d'avoir des clients, aussi bien a l'interieur qu'a l'exterieur du pays », explique-t-elle. La creatrice affirme avoir particulierement travaille sur de nouvelles techniques de tissage. Ses creations sont realisees a partir de fils de coton « bio » burkinabe, depuis la matiere premiere jusqu'a la finition. Elle estime que ces innovations permettent de depasser les motifs traditionnels pour proposer des tissus plus diversifies et rechercher davantage d'excellence dans la production locale. Le SIAO, une opportunite de developper les ventes Au-dela de la visibilite, les exposants esperent surtout transformer leur participation en opportunites commerciales. Les ventes directes et les commandes constituent des enjeux importants pour les artisans presents a Ouagadougou. C'est le cas de Diankan Mahamadou, artisan malien, qui expose une gamme d'articles en cuir destines aux femmes, aux hommes et aux enfants. Son stand propose notamment des chaussures, des sacs et des porte-monnaie. « On attend les clients, incha'Allah. Beaucoup de clients, meme », espere-t-il. Pour cet exposant, le salon represente une occasion de toucher une nouvelle clientele et d'elargir les debouches de ses produits. Des distinctions pour valoriser la creativite Le SIAO est egalement un espace de competition et de reconnaissance du savoir-faire artisanal. Certains exposants viennent avec l'ambition de decrocher des distinctions qui peuvent renforcer leur notoriete. C'est le cas de Kalizeta Ouedraogo, creatrice burkinabe specialisee dans la transformation de la calebasse. Pour sa quatrieme participation, elle presente de nouvelles realisations, apres avoir ete primee lors de ses trois precedentes editions. « En 2023, j'ai remporte le troisieme prix, en 2024 le premier prix et en 2025, j'ai egalement ete laureate », rappelle-t-elle. Ses precedentes distinctions recompensaient notamment des coupes et des chaises fabriquees a partir de calebasses. Cette annee, elle entend surprendre davantage les visiteurs avec de nouvelles creations. « On a amene d'autres materiaux, d'autres œuvres que nous avons pu fabriquer. Si on dit qu'avec la calebasse, on peut faire des lits, tant qu'on ne les voit pas, on ne peut pas y croire. Nous souhaitons vraiment remporter le premier prix cette annee encore », affirme-t-elle. Entre recherche de nouveaux clients, perspectives de partenariats et ambition de decrocher des distinctions, les attentes des artisans sont nombreuses pour cette 18ᵉ edition du SIAO. Elles rejoignent l'ambition affichee par les organisateurs a travers le theme de cette annee, consacre aux synergies entre artisanat et industrialisation pour la valorisation du patrimoine africain. items.title: 2027: Accord Party challenges suit seeking to disqualify all its candidates
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Accord Party (AP) has approached the Federal High Court in Abuja for the dismissal of a suit seeking to disqualify all its candidates for the 2027 general elections. The party, in a preliminary objection filed through a team of lawyers led by a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Mr. Musibau Adetunbi, maintained that the court lacks the jurisdiction to entertain the legal action filed by its National Secretary, Mr. Adebukola Ajaja. It argued that the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CV/2524/2026, lacked competence as it was filed outside the 14-day period allowed by law. Insisting that the action had become statute-barred, the party further contended that the issue bordered on the nomination of candidates, which it said falls within the domestic affairs of a political party and is non-justiciable. Moreover, while querying the locus standi (legal right) of the plaintiff to file the action, Accord Party noted that he is not an aspirant in the primary election it conducted on May 29. It also faulted the competence of the suit on the ground that proper parties were not included. The Accord Party argued that while the plaintiff wants the court to nullify the nomination of its candidates, none of the candidates who would be affected by the outcome of the suit were made parties, to afford them the opportunity of being heard. The party further described the suit as “premature”, arguing that the plaintiff failed to give the required 21 days’ pre-action notice. It told the court that its primary was conducted in accordance with all relevant laws and guidelines, adding that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has since recognised its outcome and the list of candidates duly submitted to the electoral umpire in the prescribed format. It further argued that, contrary to the plaintiff’s contention, the National Chairman and the National Organising Secretary could validly sign and submit candidates’ lists and forms to INEC where the National Secretary is unavailable, in line with Article 18 of the party’s constitution and Regulations 25(3) and 28(2) of INEC’s Guidelines. Accord Party added: “INEC Regulations and Guidelines for Political Parties did not in any way specify that the plaintiff herein must sign the forwarding letter, neither did the Constitution of the second defendant require her (the plaintiff) to sign. “The National Executives of the party expressly authorized the fourth defendant to co-sign with the 3rd Defendant. No wrong has been done.” Relying on the Supreme Court’s decision in Jegede v. INEC, Accord Party argued that even if only its National Chairman had signed, “the plaintiff’s case is still bound to fail because the signature of the National Chairman suffices on the authority of Jegede v. INEC.” In a counter-affidavit deposed to by its National Chairman, Maxwell Mgbudem, the party told the court that, contrary to the plaintiff’s claim that her responsibilities were usurped by the National Organising Secretary, she had actually abandoned her duties. “The plaintiff is the National Secretary, but she had stopped attending the meetings of the National Working Committee, which under our party’s constitution comprises the National Executive Officers. “She did not attend the past three consecutive National Working Committee meetings. “As the Chief Executive of the second defendant, I can sign any document on behalf of the party, except where either the National Executive Council or the Convention sees the need for the contrary. “By virtue of Article 18(1) of the Accord Constitution, I am the Chief Executive of Accord, and by virtue of 18(1)(v), I have the power to ‘assign specific functions to any member or officer of the party.’ “On 24th May, 2026, the National Working Committee, under my leadership, met and resolved that I, as the National Chairman, and Elder Ibe Kenechukwu ThankGod, the National Organising Secretary, should co-sign the forwarding letter of the aspirants who are eventually successful. “INEC recognised the primary election conducted on 29th May, 2026 by the National Executive of the party under the supervision of the National Working Committee. “After the successful completion of all the primaries into all contested elective positions, except presidential (which the party did not conduct any primary election into), I and Mr. Ibe forwarded the names of all our successful candidates electronically to INEC. “Electronic submissions of all INEC forms, other than the letters, do not require physical signing of all the forms due to the large number of participating political parties and the extremely large number of candidates participating in the 2027 General Elections,” the party added. items.title: Huit morts et 21 rescapés dans un accident de la circulation
items.description: Un accident de la circulation a endeuillé le Ghana, le jeudi 29 octobre 2026. Une collision entre un car immatriculé en Côte d’Ivoire, en route pour Cotonou, au Bénin, et un autobus burkinabè a fait huit morts et 21 rescapés sur l’autoroute N1 Elubo-Takoradi, dans l'ouest du territoire ghanéen. Les secours ghanéens sont intervenus pour évacuer les survivants, tandis qu’une enquête a été ouverte afin de déterminer les circonstances du drame. Sept passagers ont été tués sur le coup, tandis qu’une huitième personne a succombé à ses blessures après son admission à l’hôpital. Vingt et un autres occupants ont pu être secourus par les sapeurs-pompiers ghanéens. Selon les premières informations rapportées par plusieurs médias ivoiriens et ghanéens, l’accident s’est produit aux environs de 19h26, à Azuletti, près de Samenye. Le car ivoirien, immatriculé AB 415 AN, effectuait un trajet en direction de Cotonou lorsqu’il a violemment percuté l’arrière d’un autobus burkinabè portant la plaque d’immatriculation KJA-5604J. Ce dernier était immobilisé sur l’autoroute N1 Elubo-Takoradi. Alertés, les sapeurs-pompiers d’Elubo se sont rapidement déployés sur les lieux pour porter secours aux victimes. Leur intervention a permis d’extraire 21 passagers survivants, qui ont ensuite été pris en charge et évacués vers des structures sanitaires pour recevoir les soins appropriés. Les premières indications font état d'un possible stationnement dangereux de l’autobus burkinabè, qui aurait occupé une partie de la chaussée et constitué un obstacle pour les autres véhicules. Toutefois, les circonstances précises de son immobilisation, ainsi que les conditions de visibilité et de circulation au moment du drame, restent à éclaircir. Parallèlement, les premières investigations des services de secours ghanéens évoquent une éventuelle vitesse excessive du car ivoirien. Cette hypothèse pourrait également avoir contribué à la violence de l’impact. À ce stade, aucune responsabilité n’est cependant officiellement établie et les conclusions de l’enquête devront permettre de situer les éventuelles responsabilités. Au terme des opérations de secours, les blessés ont été conduits dans des établissements hospitaliers, tandis que les dépouilles des victimes décédées ont été confiées aux services de police pour les procédures d’identification et les formalités d’usage. Ce drame remet une nouvelle fois en lumière les dangers liés à la circulation sur les grands corridors routiers ouest-africains, empruntés quotidiennement par de nombreux véhicules de transport de personnes et de marchandises. Au-delà du lourd bilan humain, cet accident rappelle surtout l’importance du respect des règles de sécurité routière, notamment en matière de stationnement et de maîtrise de la vitesse. Les résultats de l’enquête ghanéenne sont désormais attendus pour établir avec précision le déroulement de cette collision meurtrière. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Huit morts et 21 rescapés dans un accident de la circulation est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: China calls for Middle East dialogue in talks with Iran, Saudi Arabia, Oman
items.description: China stepped up diplomatic efforts on Monday to resolve the Middle East crisis, urging a return to the negotiating table in back-to-back meetings with Iranian, Omani and Saudi officials in Beijing. The meetings come days after United States President Donald Trump issued a fresh war threat more than eight months into the conflict , which was triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran and has at times spilled over into neighbouring countries. Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security”, Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri Kani, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement. Wang later called for dialogue to end the conflict “while safeguarding regional energy security and the safety of shipping lanes”, as he met with Saudi National Security Adviser Musaad bin Mohammad al-Aiban. China, a top economic partner of Iran, has long sought a detente in the months-long conflict that has disrupted global shipping. Trump said on Saturday that the United States had knocked out much of Iran’s military but still has to “take care of” one or two targets, with Tehran warning of reprisals if attacked. “All parties should… in a spirit of reason and pragmatism, focus on a political solution rather than once again resorting to armed conflict,” Wang told Bagheri Kani, according to the statement. China’s foreign ministry had not previously announced the visit by Bagheri Kani to Beijing. President Xi Jinping also met Oman’s sultan for talks in Beijing on Monday — the first visit to China by the Gulf nation’s head of state since diplomatic ties were established. Xi told Haitham bin Tariq that China was ready to “contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the region”. The Chinese leader said that the Middle East should not become a “wrestling ground for major-country rivalry and geopolitical conflicts”, state news agency Xinhua reported. Later this month, Beijing will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia as part of “shuttle diplomacy visits… aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions”, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson told a news briefing.

items.title: Le parti Sawab met en garde contre les répercussions de la hausse des prix et le recul du pouvoir d’achat des citoyens
items.description: Le Parti Sawab a mis en garde contre les répercussions croissantes de la hausse des prix et de la baisse du pouvoir d'achat des citoyens, estimant que l'aggravation de l'inflation et la dépréciation de l'ouguiya constituent désormais un fardeau de plus en plus lourd pour les familles mauritaniennes, en particulier les ménages à faibles revenus. Dans un communiqué publié ce lundi et consacré à la situation de l’économie nationale et au coût élevé de la vie, le parti, représenté au Parlement, a déclaré que les hausses successives du taux d’intérêt décidées par la Banque centrale, passant de 6 % en mai 2026 à 7,25 % la semaine dernière, reflètent l’ampleur des défis économiques liés à l’inflation et à la perte de confiance dans la monnaie nationale. Le parti a critiqué ce qu’il a qualifié d’inefficacité des mesures monétaires prises par la Banque centrale pour endiguer l’inflation, soulignant que le durcissement des exigences en matière de réserves obligatoires imposées aux banques commerciales n’avait pas freiné la hausse des prix, s’appuyant sur des données qui, selon lui, figurent dans le procès-verbal du Conseil de politique monétaire, qui montrent une hausse du taux d’inflation de 8,5 % en juillet à 9,3 % en septembre, les denrées alimentaires y contribuant à hauteur d’environ 6,8 points de pourcentage. Le communiqué a souligné la forte hausse des prix des denrées alimentaires de base, citant notamment ceux des tomates, du poisson et de la viande rouge, estimant que ces augmentations ont fait de la satisfaction des besoins alimentaires quotidiens un défi croissant pour des centaines de milliers de familles et ont transformé les repas des plus démunis en un fardeau financier dépassant leurs capacités. Le Parti Sawab a estimé que la hausse continue du coût de la vie aggrave les souffrances des familles mauritaniennes et affaiblit leur capacité à subvenir à leurs besoins fondamentaux, appelant à remédier aux déséquilibres économiques qui se répercutent directement sur la vie quotidienne des citoyens.

items.title: Dawajine 2026 se penche sur l’avenir de la filière à l’horizon 2030
items.description: La 27e édition du Salon Dawajine se tiendra du 3 au 5 novembre 2026 au Centre d’expositions Mohammed VI à El Jadida, sous le thème « L’aviculture marocaine au rendez-vous de 2030 » . Placé sous le Haut Patronage du Roi Mohammed VI, l’événement réunira plus de 200 exposants et devrait accueillir près de 12.000 visiteurs. Organisé par la Fédération interprofessionnelle du secteur avicole (FISA), ce rendez-vous professionnel entend mettre en lumière les perspectives de développement de la filière avicole nationale, dans un contexte marqué par les enjeux de souveraineté alimentaire, de compétitivité et de durabilité. L’inauguration officielle est prévue mercredi 4 novembre, sous la présidence de Khalid Hatimy, ministre de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime et de la Souveraineté alimentaire. Durant trois jours, le salon proposera plusieurs rencontres professionnelles ainsi que la présentation de produits et services à travers quelque 300 marques marocaines et étrangères. Il constituera également un espace d’échange d’expertises, de développement de partenariats et d’exploration de nouvelles opportunités d’investissement. Cette édition entend notamment favoriser une réflexion collective sur l’avenir de la filière à l’horizon 2030 et renforcer la coopération entre les opérateurs marocains et leurs partenaires internationaux, particulièrement dans le cadre de la coopération Sud-Sud. items.title: La Guinée inaugure sa première raffinerie d’or pour renforcer sa souveraineté minière
items.description: Le president guineen Mamadi Doumbouya a inaugure, le 1er novembre, la Nimba Gold Refinery (NGR), premiere raffinerie d'or du pays, situee a Gbessia, dans la capitale Conakry. Avec cette installation, les autorites entendent developper la transformation locale des ressources minieres et mieux maîtriser la filiere aurifere. Jusqu'a present, une grande partie de l'or guineen etait exportee a l'etat brut pour etre raffinee a l'etranger. Le pays ne profitait donc pas pleinement de la valeur ajoutee liee a cette activite. Pour changer cette situation, le gouvernement avait annonce en juin l'interdiction des exportations d'or brut et l'obligation de proceder a son raffinage sur le territoire national. Lors de l'inauguration, le ministre des Mines, Bouna Sylla, a salue ce changement de cap. « Depuis des siecles, la Guinee a exploite et exporte l'or a l'etat brut », a-t-il rappele, soulignant qu'une partie de la richesse generee par le raffinage echappait jusqu'ici a l'economie nationale. La nouvelle raffinerie affiche une capacite theorique de traitement de 733 tonnes d'or par an, bien superieure aux volumes actuellement produits dans le pays. Sa direction estime qu'en fonctionnant a la moitie de cette capacite, elle pourrait generer un flux financier annuel de 4,5 milliards de dollars. Ce montant reste une projection et ne correspond pas a un benefice net garanti. L'installation doit egalement favoriser la creation d'emplois qualifies, la formation de techniciens guineens et une meilleure tracabilite de l'or. L'orpaillage artisanal, un defi majeur Cette strategie se heurte toutefois a un defi de taille : le controle de la production artisanale, qui represente l'essentiel de l'or extrait dans le pays. Sur les quelque 70 tonnes exportees en 2025, pres de 50 tonnes provenaient de l'orpaillage artisanal. Une partie de cet or echappe encore a l'administration miniere et transite par des pays voisins, notamment le Mali, avant d'etre exportee. Cette difficulte a notamment ete soulignee par Oumar Totiya Barry, directeur de l'Observatoire guineen des mines et des metaux. La reorganisation de la filiere concerne egalement les entreprises minieres. L'etat prevoit ainsi d'acheter, en francs guineens, jusqu'a 30 % de la production des societes industrielles et semi-industrielles. Cette mesure doit notamment contribuer au renforcement des reserves de change de la Banque centrale et a la stabilite economique du pays. La transformation locale gagne du terrain en Afrique de l'Ouest La Guinee rejoint ainsi d'autres pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest qui cherchent a valoriser davantage leurs ressources minieres sur leur territoire. C'est notamment le cas du Burkina Faso, qui a inaugure sa premiere raffinerie d'or en septembre. Cette orientation ne se limite toutefois pas a l'or. La Guinee, qui figure parmi les principaux producteurs mondiaux de bauxite, cherche egalement a developper sa transformation sur place. Trois raffineries d'alumine sont actuellement en construction. a travers ces projets, les autorites guineennes veulent renforcer l'industrie nationale, reduire progressivement leur dependance aux exportations de matieres premieres brutes et conserver une plus grande part de la richesse issue de leur sous-sol.

items.title: Éliminatoires CAN 2027 : Amadou Diawara parmi les 25 joueurs convoqués par Paulo Duarte
items.description: Le sélectionneur national de Guinée, Paulo Duarte, a dévoilé ce lundi 2 novembre, la liste des 25 joueurs retenus pour la double confrontation face à l’Érythrée, comptant pour les 3 ᵉ et 4 ᵉ journées des éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) 2027. Une sélection marquée par la présence de plusieurs cadres du Syli national, mais aussi par le retour d’Amadou Diawara, longtemps absent du groupe. Pour ces deux rendez-vous importants, le technicien portugais a renouvelé sa confiance à plusieurs de ses habituels titulaires. Serhou Guirassy et Aliou Badara Baldé figurent notamment parmi les joueurs convoqués pour conduire l'attaque guinéenne. L'autre fait marquant de cette liste est le retour d'Amadou Diawara. Le milieu de terrain retrouve ainsi le groupe du Syli national à un moment important de la campagne qualificative. Cette double confrontation revêt un enjeu particulier pour la Guinée, qui entend consolider sa position dans le groupe D et se rapprocher de la qualification pour la phase finale de la CAN 2027. La première manche, comptant pour la 3 ᵉ journée, est prévue le 12 novembre prochain au stade du 28 septembre de Conakry. Le Syli national jouera face à son public pour tenter de décrocher une victoire à domicile. Quatre jours plus tard, soit le 16 novembre, les deux équipes se retrouveront pour la manche retour, prévue au Caire, en Égypte. Au classement du groupe D, l'Afrique du Sud occupe la première place avec 6 points. La Guinée suit à la deuxième position avec 3 unités, tandis que le Kenya et l'Érythrée ferment la marche avec un seul point. Avec cette liste de 25 joueurs, Paulo Duarte mise sur un mélange d'expérience et de continuité pour négocier au mieux ces deux rencontres et permettre au Syli national de rester dans la course à la qualification pour la CAN 2027. items.title: The tragic death of Javits Frimpong: Let us confront bullying without turning it into a black-on-black racial divide
items.description: The tragic death of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, a Ghanaian teenager who was fatally shot while walking to school in the Bronx, New York, is a painful reminder of how vulnerable our children can be and how urgently we need to confront bullying, youth violence and the safety of students in our schools and communities. Javits had moved from Ghana to the United States to reunite with his father and begin a new chapter of his life. Like many African immigrant parents, his father must have brought him to America with the hope of giving him better opportunities, access to quality education and a brighter future. Sadly, that dream has been cut short in the most heartbreaking circumstances. Reports indicate that Javits had experienced bullying at school and that his father had raised concerns with school authorities. At least two students were reportedly suspended following incidents involving the teenager. His father believes the shooting may have been connected to the bullying. However, the police have not established a connection between the school incidents and the killing, and the circumstances surrounding the shooting remain under investigation. We must therefore demand a thorough investigation, accountability for whoever is responsible and appropriate support for the bereaved family. No parent should have to bury a 15-year-old child under such circumstances. But beyond the immediate tragedy, I believe there is an important conversation we, particularly African immigrant communities in America, must approach with care and maturity. There is a need for African immigrants to be careful about how we frame conversations surrounding bullying in American public schools, particularly incidents involving African immigrant children and African-American children. I understand the anxiety and frustration within our communities. Parents who bring their children from Africa to America expect them to enjoy the opportunities, security and protection that should come with growing up in a country that promises equal opportunity. When an African immigrant child experiences bullying, discrimination or hostility, it is understandable that parents and community members will be concerned. However, we must be careful not to frame every such incident as a confrontation between Black Americans and Black Africans. Doing so risks creating a racial division that does not address the underlying problem and could unnecessarily deepen tensions between two communities that share much more in common than what separates them. Bullying is not an exclusively African-American problem, nor is it a problem that occurs only between African-American and African immigrant children. It is a broader social and educational problem that affects children across racial, ethnic and cultural backgrounds. There are well-known instances of Black children being bullied in predominantly White schools. There are also instances of immigrant children being bullied by other immigrant children, and of children from different racial backgrounds bullying one another. The common denominator is bullying, not necessarily race. We should therefore avoid allowing the circumstances surrounding Javits’ death to become an indictment of an entire racial or ethnic community. The identities, motives and possible connections of those responsible for his death must be established through a proper investigation, not assumptions or collective blame. If we turn this tragedy into an African-versus-African-American debate, we risk losing sight of the real issue: the safety of our children and the culture of bullying and violence that must be confronted. Bullying can take many forms. It may be physical, verbal, psychological, social or cyber-based. It can involve racial insults, hostility towards someone’s accent, ridicule of their background, exclusion because of their cultural identity or repeated intimidation. One aspect of bullying that we sometimes overlook is that teachers themselves can also become victims of bullying, particularly from students. Teachers, especially those from African, Caribbean backgrounds and Hispanic backgrounds, may sometimes face intimidation, disrespect, ridicule and other forms of hostility from students who exploit cultural differences, accents or unfamiliarity with certain aspects of the American school environment. I speak from personal experience. I was once a high school teacher in New York, where I taught Algebra 2, Trigonometry and Pre-Calculus. These are not the easiest subjects to teach, particularly because many students already have a phobia of mathematics and approach these subjects with anxiety and reluctance. During my time in the classroom, I experienced situations where some students attempted to bully and intimidate me. Had I not lived in the United States for several years before entering the teaching profession, I might have found the experience extremely frustrating and probably walked away from the job. Teaching in an American high school requires more than subject knowledge. You must understand the school culture, the students’ behaviour, the education system and how to manage different personalities in a classroom. You also need to know how to establish authority without turning every disagreement into a confrontation. Despite those challenges, teaching became one of the most rewarding careers I had in the United States. It gave me a firsthand understanding of how the American education system works, the challenges teachers encounter and the importance of parental involvement in a child’s education. More importantly, it taught me valuable lessons about how to prepare and raise my own children as they navigate the American school system. I share this experience to make a broader point that bullying is not always a simple matter of one racial group targeting another. It can take different forms, involve different people and occur in different relationships. Students bully other students, and sometimes students bully teachers. Teachers can also mistreat students. The issue requires us to look beyond racial assumptions and examine the behaviour, culture and circumstances that allow bullying to thrive. This is why our conversations must be balanced. We should listen to children, support teachers, hold schools accountable and ensure that everyone within the educational environment is treated with dignity and respect. An African child who has recently arrived in America may have to adjust to a new environment, a different educational system, unfamiliar social expectations and sometimes a different way of speaking. Such children may become targets of ridicule because of their accents, cultural practices, clothing or unfamiliarity with certain aspects of American life. Schools must take these experiences seriously. At the same time, we must recognise that African-American children also experience bullying, including in predominantly White educational environments. Their experiences deserve the same attention, empathy and seriousness. The solution cannot be to encourage African immigrant children to see African-American children as their adversaries, or vice versa. It must be to create school environments where every child, irrespective of race, nationality, ethnicity or immigration background, feels safe, respected and protected. Schools must establish effective reporting systems, investigate complaints promptly, protect students who report bullying from retaliation and engage parents when incidents occur. Disciplinary action should also be accompanied by appropriate counselling, monitoring and interventions that address the behaviour responsible for the problem. Parents equally have a responsibility to teach their children respect, tolerance, self-control and peaceful conflict resolution. We cannot demand that schools do everything while ignoring the influence of the home and the wider community. African immigrants must understand that our experiences in America are connected to a much larger Black experience. African-Americans have their own history, struggles, sacrifices and contributions to American society. African immigrants also bring their histories, cultures, aspirations and experiences. We may have different cultural backgrounds, accents, traditions and migration experiences, but those differences should not become reasons for hostility. There may be genuine tensions and cultural misunderstandings between some African immigrants and African-American children. Those issues should be acknowledged and addressed honestly rather than dismissed. However, acknowledging such tensions is different from portraying an entire community as hostile towards another. We must also be careful about the language we use on social media. A tragedy involving one child must not become an opportunity to circulate unverified accusations, generalise about an entire racial group or encourage resentment. More troubling is the fact that some people are willing to turn Javits’ tragic death into an argument about why Africans should remain in Africa rather than migrate to the United States. That alone tells you why we must learn to ignore certain people, regardless of how many there are or how loudly they express their idiotic views. To exploit the death of a 15-year-old boy to discourage others from pursuing opportunities abroad is deeply insensitive. Such thinking demonstrates a shocking absence of empathy, emotional intelligence and, quite frankly, basic common sense. There is a time for debate and a time to show compassion. A grieving family deserves our sympathy, not an opportunity for people to advance their personal agendas. We can have honest conversations about the challenges of raising children in America, school safety, migration and the realities of life abroad without using someone’s death as a platform for insensitive commentary. We can demand justice for Javits without blaming African-Americans collectively. We can condemn bullying without creating racial divisions. We can demand that schools protect immigrant children while recognising that every child, including African-American children, deserves the same protection. Our position must be against bullying, discrimination, intimidation and youth violence, regardless of who commits them or who becomes the victim. The death of Javits Frimpong should prompt serious questions about school safety, bullying prevention, access to firearms, youth violence and the responsibilities of parents, schools and community institutions. We must establish whether the bullying he reportedly experienced had any connection to his killing. We must also insist that the authorities investigate the circumstances thoroughly and bring anyone responsible to justice. But we must not allow grief and anger to lead us into a narrative that divides Black Americans and Africans. That would be an unfortunate outcome of an already devastating tragedy. A 15-year-old boy lost his life. A father has lost his son. A mother in Ghana has lost her child. A family has been plunged into grief, and a community is searching for answers. Javits deserved to live, to learn, to make friends, to pursue his dreams and to experience the opportunities his parents hoped America would offer him. Let this tragedy strengthen our resolve to protect every child, regardless of where that child comes from. Justice for Javits Frimpong. An end to bullying. An end to youth violence. And a united commitment to the safety and dignity of all our children. – Alhaji Baba Suwari STEM Advocate Executive Member of Yankasa Association USA Bronx, New York alhajisuwari@gmail.com

items.title: La hausse des frais universitaires pour les étudiants non Européens en France est «discriminatoire»
items.description: C'est une rentrée particulière pour les étudiants africains en France. Depuis septembre, les frais d'inscription dans les universités en France ont été multipliés par seize. Un tarif qui s'applique uniquement aux étudiants étrangers extracommunautaires, c'est-à-dire hors Union européenne. Désormais, les étudiants non Européens doivent débourser l'équivalent du salaire français moyen. Une mesure dont pâtissent en premier lieu les ressortissants africains, qui représentent près de la moitié des étudiants étrangers en France. Le Tchadien Hamit Wachi Allatchi, président du Collectif des étudiants extracommunautaires de l'université de Strasbourg, est l'invité d'Afrique Midi.

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs series
items.description: Dear CEO, Welcome to November, the penultimate month of 2026. As the year approaches its close, CEOs must intensify their focus on performance delivery, financial discipline, organizational accountability, and strategic readiness for 2027. November is an important leadership month. It provides an opportunity to address outstanding performance gaps, strengthen executive coordination, protect organizational value, and ensure that the new year begins with clarity and purpose. Throughout this month, the Daily Insight for CEOs Series will examine five important leadership themes designed to help CEOs lead the final stretch of 2026 effectively. NOVEMBER 2026 THEMES WEEK 1: Year-End Performance, Execution & Accountability November 2–6 Monday, November 2: The CEO’s Role in Driving Year-End Performance Focus on accelerating performance and ensuring that the organization’s most important year-end commitments receive leadership attention. Tuesday, November 3: Closing Performance Gaps Before Year-End Identify underperforming areas, address execution challenges, and implement corrective actions before the year closes. Wednesday, November 4: Executive Accountability for Results Strengthen ownership, performance monitoring, and accountability across the executive leadership team. Thursday, November 5: Improving Operational Efficiency Before Year-End Identify inefficiencies, reduce waste, improve productivity, and strengthen operational discipline. Friday, November 6: Finishing 2026 Strong: The CEO’s Leadership Agenda Align people, resources, and priorities to deliver the organization’s most important remaining objectives. WEEK 2: Financial Performance, Cash Flow & Business Sustainability November 9–13 Monday, November 9: The CEO’s Responsibility for Financial Performance Strengthen executive attention to financial results, profitability, cash flow, and financial sustainability. Tuesday, November 10: Cash Flow Management as a Strategic Leadership Priority Protect liquidity, improve cash conversion, and strengthen financial resilience. Wednesday, November 11: Strengthening Profit Margins and Cost Discipline Improve profitability through pricing discipline, productivity, cost control, and better resource utilization. Thursday, November 12: Managing Financial Risks and Business Exposure Identify financial vulnerabilities, anticipate emerging risks, and strengthen financial controls. Friday, November 13: Building Financial Resilience for 2027 Position the organization to enter the new year with a stronger financial foundation and disciplined investment priorities. WEEK 3: Governance, Risk Management & Institutional Leadership November 16–20 Monday, November 16: The CEO’s Role in Strengthening Corporate Governance Reinforce transparency, accountability, ethical leadership, and effective board-management relationships. Tuesday, November 17: Enterprise Risk Management as a Leadership Responsibility Integrate risk awareness into strategic planning, executive decisions, and organizational performance. Wednesday, November 18: Building a Culture of Integrity and Ethical Leadership Establish leadership standards that promote trust, responsible conduct, and institutional credibility. Thursday, November 19: Business Continuity and Organizational Resilience Prepare the organization to manage disruptions, protect critical operations, and maintain essential services. Friday, November 20: Strengthening Stakeholder Confidence and Trust Build lasting confidence among employees, customers, investors, regulators, partners, and the wider business community. WEEK 4: People, Culture & Leadership Continuity November 23–27 Monday, November 23: The CEO’s Role in Strengthening Organizational Culture Shape the values, behaviours, and leadership practices that influence organizational performance. Tuesday, November 24: Developing the Next Generation of Leaders Build leadership pipelines, strengthen succession readiness, and prepare emerging leaders for greater responsibility. Wednesday, November 25: Retaining Critical Talent and Institutional Knowledge Protect essential capabilities by strengthening employee engagement, development, and knowledge continuity. Thursday, November 26: Building a Culture of Ownership and High Performance Encourage responsibility, collaboration, initiative, and consistent delivery across the organization. Friday, November 27: Preparing the Organization for Leadership Continuity Strengthen succession arrangements, management systems, and institutional capacity for sustainable performance. WEEK 5: Strategic Reflection & Final Preparation for 2027 November 30 Monday, November 30: The CEO’s Strategic Review Before the Final Month of 2026 Assess the organization’s progress, identify outstanding priorities, and establish the leadership agenda for December and the transition into 2027. WHY THIS MATTERS November is a decisive month for executive leadership. The CEO must ensure that the organization does not lose focus as the year approaches its end. Financial performance must be protected, accountability strengthened, risks managed, people developed, and strategic priorities aligned with the demands of 2027. The responsibility is to finish 2026 with discipline while ensuring that the organization is institutionally, financially, and strategically prepared for the future. Let’s lead November with accountability, financial discipline, strong governance, and purposeful leadership. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: «Remigration» : l’État interdit les rassemblements, les organisateurs tiennent bon
items.description: Au cœur d'une fin de semaine marquee par des manifestations violentes , un autre match s'est joue avec l'executif. Des le 29 octobre, a la demande du ministre francais de l'Interieur Laurent Nuñez, les prefets des Hauts-de-Seine et de Paris ont interdit le colloque « Remigration : ouvrons le debat », prevu le 31 octobre au Plessis-Robinson par l'association Polemia, ainsi que la manifestation du 1er novembre a Paris, portee par le collectif Objectif Remigration. Les arretes invoquaient des « risques de troubles a l'ordre public », notamment a la suite de l'attentat de Trappes. Une decision contestee au nom des libertes publiques Jean-Yves Le Gallou, ancien haut fonctionnaire et president de Polemia, a immediatement denonce une « formidable atteinte a la liberte d'expression » et un « delire liberticide ». Un refere-liberte a ete depose en urgence devant le tribunal administratif. Il a ete rejete. Les organisateurs ont alors choisi de tenir le colloque en ligne, depuis les studios du media independant Radio Courtoisie, avec des interventions diffusees sur YouTube. 🔴 EN DIRECT : Suivez l'événement « France Remigration - ouvrons le débat » sur Radio Courtoisie https://t.co/6Zx2gpfZau — Radio Courtoisie (@radiocourtoisie) October 31, 2026 Plusieurs personnalites ont pu s'exprimer, meme si le colloque n'a pas eu lieu sur place. Parmi les intervenants sollicites, eric Zemmour, candidat a la presidentielle a revendique etre le seul a proposer un ministere de la remigration. 🔴 Éric Zemmour : "Je suis le seul à proposer un ministère de la Remigration" Bruno Retailleau sur la Remigration : "C’est stupide" Marine Le Pen sur la Remigration : "C’est injuste et antirépublicain" Voici le discours complet d’Éric Zemmour au colloque de la Remigration. — Baby Lone (@Babylone771) November 1, 2026 Malgre l'arrete prefectoral visant aussi les reunions du collectif, une rencontre s'est tenue dimanche dans un restaurant parisien du 15e arrondissement. Les participants, dûment filtres, ont poursuivi les discussions sur le sujet. Les organisateurs affirment que l'interdiction n'a pas empeche le debat d'avoir lieu. C’est maintenant ! Personne ne nous empêchera de nous exprimer ! — Logan Djian (@LoganDjian) November 1, 2026 Les initiateurs du colloque soulignent que la liberte de se reunir et de discuter d'idees politiques, meme controversees, constitue un pilier democratique, et qu'interdire un colloque dans un lieu prive au nom de l'ordre public ouvre une breche preoccupante. Le concept de « remigration », retour planifie de certaines populations vers leur pays d'origine, continue d'etre debattu. Il ne fait cependant pas l'unanimite a droite. Le depute Jean-Philippe Tanguy a ainsi fustige celui-ci, se placant en plus-disant du macronisme et suggerant l'interdiction des organisations qui denoncent la notion de « Grand remplacement ». .@JphTanguy défend désormais sur le Grand Remplacement, qui est une réalité chiffrée et statistiquement prouvée et annoncée (40% des naissances en 2050 origine immigré et 50 % de la population en 2070), un point de vue repris de la gauche. Ce n'est pas le réel qui est à prendre en compte selon lui, mais le fait que ce sont des lanceurs d'alerte de droite qui en diffusent l'inquiétante réalité. Plutôt que d'argumenter sur le bien fondé ou non de ce constat, Tanguy préfère le nier, comme la gauche. Il justifie donc toutes les mesures de police et les abus d'interprétation du droit d'une magistrature politisée qui participe de la négation des dangers sécuritaires de l'immigration. En ce sens il approuve donc la pensée et les actes de Darmanin et Macron. Pour un député du RN c'est assez scandaleux. — Pascal Gannat #Conservateur #Libertés #DSE (@PGannat) October 31, 2026 Les organisateurs se felicitent d'avoir pu se rassembler malgre tout. Jean-Yves Le Gallou resume ainsi : « Si l'on veut que les peuples historiques restent majoritaires sur la terre de leurs ancetres et gardent la joie de vivre entre soi dans une societe de confiance, il n'y a pas d'autre alternative que la remigration. »

items.title: Cape Coast Communique: Democracy Is Not For Sale
items.description: ISSUED BY THE DEMOCRACY NOT FOR SALE PROJECT (JOYNEWS IMPACT MAKERS FOUNDATION, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH ADOM BRANDS /MULTIMEDIA GROUP) CAPE COAST — FRIDAY, OCTOBER 30, 2026 This communiqué is issued following the Democracy Not for Sale dialogue held at the Centre for National Culture, Cape Coast, on Friday, October 30, 2026, at 4:00 PM. The event marked the sixth edition of the Democracy Not for Sale series overall, and the third hosted by the Adom brands: Adom TV, Asempa 94.7FM, Adom Online, and Nhyira 104.5FM, in partnership with the JoyNews Impact Makers Foundation. The programme combined a field survey of residents across Cape Coast with a stakeholder dialogue bringing together civic education, electoral administration, academia, local government, and party politics, to examine the influence of money on Ghana’s democratic processes and to chart a path toward cleaner, more issue-based elections. Survey Findings Fieldwork in Cape Coast recorded over 350 interactions, yielding 193 structured respondents, well above the ideal sample size of 150 calculated for the Central Region using a weight of 0.094 derived from the 2021 Population and Housing Census. The study forms part of a national target of 1,600 respondents across 10 regions, at a 95% confidence level with a margin of error of ±2.45%. Scale of field engagement in Cape Coast. Respondents were 53% male and 47% female, with an age profile skewed markedly young: half of all respondents (50%) were between 18 and 25 years old, reflecting Cape Coast’s large student population. Gender distribution of respondents. Age distribution of respondents. Awareness of Vote Buying 99% of respondents had some awareness of vote buying — 27.5% having personally witnessed a candidate offering money or gifts for votes, and 71.5% having heard reliable reports — with only 1% reporting no awareness at all. Awareness of candidates offering money or gifts for votes. Witnessed versus heard reports, by occupation. Money’s Influence — A Generational Reversal Cape Coast produced a striking reversal of the pattern seen elsewhere in the project: only 10.31% of 18–25-year-olds, half the entire sample — rated money’s influence on election outcomes as high, against 89.69% who rated it low. The share rating money’s influence as high rose with age, reaching 50% among both the 36–50 and 51+ cohorts. Perceived influence of money on election outcomes, by age group. Willingness to Vote on Ideas Over Money 91.7% of respondents said they would vote for a candidate with less money but better ideas — the highest such figure recorded under the project — and this commitment held consistently across every age group, from 85% among 26–35-year-olds to 92.86% among 36–50-year-olds. Willingness to vote for a candidate with less money but better ideas. Who Finances Political Campaigns 74% of respondents — the highest figure recorded under the project — identified government money or taxpayer funds as the primary hidden financier of political campaigns, followed by politicians’ personal savings (29%), wealthy businessmen (11%), and organised crime or illicit groups (8%). Perceived “hidden” financiers of political campaigns. Confidence in the Law Across every age group, the near-universal view was that Ghana’s laws exist but are not enforced — reaching 100% agreement among 36–50 year-olds. Confidence in the strength and enforcement of current laws, by age group. What Would Stop It Asked what would most effectively stop “democracy for sale,” 46% of respondents said nothing can be done — the largest single response, and the first time this view has outranked all others under the project — ahead of improving standard of living (37%) and strict jail time for vote-buyers and vote-sellers (29%). Perceived most effective way to stop “democracy for sale.” The Dialogue The panel for the Cape Coast dialogue comprised Mercy Essien (Regional Director, NCCE), Gloria Boahemaa Asante (Director, Electoral Commission, Cape Coast), Professor Jonathan Asante Otchere (Executive Director, African Institute of Strategic Studies, and Political Science Lecturer, University of Cape Coast), George Justice Acquah (Municipal Chief Executive, Cape Coast), and Takyi Mensah (Regional Secretary, New Patriotic Party). Mercy Essien defended the NCCE’s continuing constitutional mandate to explain and guide the public on civic responsibilities, while Gloria Boahemaa Asante stressed the Electoral Commission’s institutional commitment to fairness, ensuring neither party is unilaterally favoured. Professor Jonathan Asante Otchere offered the dialogue’s sharpest structural diagnosis: vote buying persists because both givers and receivers sustain it, worsened in his view by Ghana’s delegate system, under which far more resources are now shared to influence delegates than in the early 1990s. He named economic hardship, greed, and a weak regulatory framework as the three principal drivers, and argued that party sanctions against offending candidates remain too weak to deter the practice. George Justice Acquah, the Municipal Chief Executive, declared that “our conscience is not for sale, your rights are not for sale, but that is what we are seeing here in Ghana,” arguing the practice has spread into churches, community groups, and union leadership, and that responsibility is shared across society rather than resting with politicians alone. He called for clearer party policies, less politicisation of public discourse, and sustained education on patriotism. Takyi Mensah, speaking for the NPP, traced vote buying to a trust deficit: politicians who fail to deliver on promises prompt citizens to extract something tangible before they even gain power. He called on parties to show genuine resolve in disciplining members who engage in the practice. Recommendations Strengthen internal party discipline and sanctions against candidates and members who engage in vote buying, consistent with the dialogue’s call for parties to show genuine resolve rather than tolerance. Reform aspects of the delegate system identified as having measurably worsened vote buying at the primary and internal-party stage since the early 1990s. Build a stronger regulatory framework governing political campaign financing, with clearer rules on permissible contributions and spending. Sustain and expand NCCE and Electoral Commission civic education efforts, given that the Commission’s mandate remains central to public understanding of electoral integrity. Invest in addressing the economic hardship identified by panelists as a root driver of both the giving and taking of money for votes. Promote sustained public education on patriotism, shared civic responsibility, and the depoliticisation of everyday public discourse. Make political party policies and platforms clearer and more accessible to the electorate, to support the public’s strong stated preference for voting on ideas over money. Address the pronounced public fatalism recorded in this survey — the view that “nothing can be done” — through visible, sustained enforcement action that demonstrates the laws against vote buying can and will be applied. Conclusion The Cape Coast edition of Democracy Not for Sale surfaces a distinctive and, in places, encouraging profile: a youngest generation that is both the least convinced that money determines electoral outcomes and among the most committed to voting on ideas regardless of cost. Yet this sits alongside near-total awareness of vote buying, the strongest public attribution of political financing to government resources recorded anywhere in the project, and the most pronounced strand of public fatalism yet recorded, with a plurality concluding the practice cannot be stopped at all. The panel’s recommendations- stronger party discipline, delegate-system reform, sustained civic education, and visible enforcement, point toward addressing both halves of this gap: giving institutional substance to the public’s stated preference for ideas over money, while confronting directly the sense of resignation that currently coexists with it. The Democracy Not for Sale project will continue to track these dynamics as the dialogue series moves to further regions across Ghana. For more information on the Democracy Not for Sale project, contact the JoyNews Impact Makers Foundation

items.title: Peter Ansah: Three lessons from Africa’s inaugural Climate x Culture Summit
items.description: On Thursday, 22 October, at the Accra A.I. Community Centre, at the Google Office, musicians, festival directors, climate scientists, bankers, journalists and policy officials gathered for the first Climate x Culture Summit. Professionals and practitioners from two worlds that rarely share a stage were in the same room. The question was simple: can entertainment and cultural experiences be designed and executed more sustainably? It was a full day of panels and keynotes covering creativity, festivals, financing and storytelling. Leading the conversation were people who have built the industry’s biggest experiences and its most innovative alternatives. Culture entrepreneur and founder of the Rave Group was Afro Nation Ghana’s executive producer when the international Afrobeats festival first touched Ghana’s shores in 2019. His teams at The Rave Group and Republic of Amusement have turned waste dumps into festival sites, planned raves in nature, and routinely set aside funds for innovative waste management solutions during festivals. Joseph Zotoo is a senior business development and research lead at The OR Foundation, a Ghana-based organisation working on the problem of used-clothing waste. It was clear from the start of the Climate X Culture summit. This was not going to be a talking shop but a day of celebration of impact and experience sharing. Three lessons stood out. 1. Culture cannot be an afterthought of climate action “What if the next big climate solution is in a song, on a stage, in a story or in the way we produce the events we love?” That’s how Prisilla Adomaah Nsonwaah from the Centre for Scientific Research, West Africa, began her presentation at the Climate X Culture Summit. The premise is that culture is where the message and impact of climate action are seen, heard, felt and lived the most. Cultural products like songs, films, games, outfits, installations and experiences reach audiences that policy papers do not. UN estimates put the global creative economy at more than $2tn in annual revenue and nearly 50 million jobs. Yet Africa accounted for only 1.5% of that economy in 2023, according to Brookings. The sector’s reach is large, and so is its room to grow. If climate action is to mean more than it does now, it has to enter culture, not stand outside it. 2. A Sustainable Events Industry Requires A United Front Sustainability in Ghana’s festival sector is neither a hoax nor a fantasy. Many operators across the country have been doing their bit to tackle waste. But as Ruddy Kwakye observed in his solidarity message, the effort is fragmented; the industry tends to “subdivide ourselves into smaller spaces” and “become tinier instead of combining to become bigger”. So much is being done in siloes. Consider why that matters. A festival draws 100,000 people to a city. It is a win for the promoter and the industry. The organiser spends a little more on sanitation and hires extra waste pickers; nothing is left on the ground, and everyone applauds. But that waste has to go somewhere. A weekend of 100,000 revellers can strain a landfill that never expected the load. As the landfill struggles to cope, the tricycle collector who services the neighbourhood waits longer to offload. The longer he waits, the greater the temptation to cut corners and leave refuse at the roadside. During Detty December, Ghana’s end-of-year festive season of back-to-back events, who is measuring the cumulative effect on the city’s waste system? The scale of the problem is poorly documented. Ghana generates roughly 840,000 tonnes of plastic waste a year, of which about 9.5% is collected for recycling. Other estimates are higher: some studies put annual plastic waste at 1.1 to 1.3 million tonnes. Kwakye was candid about the weakness of the data, describing the 840,000 figure as “a projection of a projection of a projection”. Without reliable counts, he argued, there is nothing for policymakers to plan around. His first rule for organisers: count honestly. Report 50 people if 50 came, and 500 if 500 did. The author, Peter Ansah and his co-panelists at Climate x Culture Summit in Accra This is where we need imagination and rethinking beyond the usual solutions of installing more waste bins at festivals. How do we stop waste way before it enters the venue, or turn festival waste into wages, leave the site as you found it, and cut noise and diesel generator use? How do we even codify and index our footprint, generating accurate festival data points that policy can plan around? Sustainability planning for festivals starts way before your first ticket gets sold and long after teardown. It means building shared systems and a common way to measure the footprint of events, so that one promoter’s good practice does not become another town’s problem. 3. Yes, we can design sustainable experiences. But who pays? Green financing decides whether any of these initiatives scale. The creative sector is large but chronically under-financed, and a greener operation costs more at the start. Japan offers a revealing comparison. Its supporters have been seen tidying stadiums since the 1998 World Cup, and they did it again after the 2-2 draw with the Netherlands in Dallas this June. But the fans bring their own bin bags. The tradition works because the cost and the habit are carried by the public and other private bodies. Ghana cannot count on that. Who pays for the bags, the sorting and the collection? What incentive does a festival operator have to adopt low-waste site design, from permaculture landscaping to reusable infrastructure? Policy may offer part of an answer. Ghana’s Green Finance Taxonomy is West Africa’s first national green taxonomy, and the Ministry of Finance released its first phase in October 2024. Its screening criteria centre on areas such as renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, green urban development, biodiversity conservation and ecotourism. Whether festivals and experience providers can use it to reduce the perceived risk of green investment has yet to be tested. Art and culture cannot replace investments or policy. It is only an access point, as argued by Eric Lartey of the World Resources Institute, meant to be leveraged for the greater good of humanity. There is significant evidence that creative and culture businesses can lead climate action. The sector’s weight deserves a seat at the table where climate policy and finance are decided. Beyond proving that, the Climate X Culture summit’s organisers, CultureJoint, have promised an Accra Accord and Sustainable Event Production Guide to help turn its conversations and recommendations into action. The real test, for the short term, is whether, come the first weekend of Detty December, someone is counting. The author, Peter Ansah, is a strategist and culture journalist from Accra, with over a decade in media, MarCom, and festivals. He has written, contributed and produced content for platforms including Brut, MusicInAfrica, and Legit Media. Working with top brands in entertainment and culture like Afro Nation, Morgan Heritage, and the, Peter brings a global perspective to his work, which has also proven useful in start-up environments where he acts as a multi-hyphenate and builds systems.
